title: [Quantization] Keep deleted and renamed params registered after process_weights_after_loading
body:
## Overview

Part 3 of 3 of keeping the loaded parameter objects through `process_weights_after_loading` (PWAL). After #62326 and #62405 (both merged), a loaded param can still disappear when PWAL deletes or renames it. This PR keeps those params registered, so after PWAL every loader-visible param is still registered under the same name, as the same object, and keeps its loaded data unless that would cost real memory.

## Claims

- **Renames alias one param under both names.** The new `move_parameter(layer, src, dst)` registers the `src` param object under `dst` as well and records `dst` as its runtime name. The loader writes through the checkpoint name and kernels read the runtime name, both pointing at one storage, so a later `replace_parameter` on either name updates both and no extra memory is used. This covers:
  - compressed-tensors `*_weight_packed` (linear, NVFP4/MXFP4/W4A8 MoE);
  - INC MXFP4;
  - the NVFP4 MoE oracle;
  - Humming NVFP4 and Humming's checkpoint-to-standard renames;
  - compressed-tensors W8A16 block FP8, which now aliases `weight_scale_inv` to `weight_scale`.
- **Loaded params no kernel reads keep their data and are marked retired** (`retire_parameter`). This covers:
  - consumed NVFP4 per-tensor scales (ModelOpt, Quark);
  - small Humming leftovers (at most 1/256 of the largest converted tensor);
  - the input scales of ModelOpt and Quark NVFP4 MoE when a weight-only backend (Marlin, Humming) is selected. These used to be set to `None`, which unregistered them. The method now leaves them registered and passes `None` to the MoE quant config.
- **Large released sources stay registered with empty storage** (`replace_parameter(layer, name, t.new_empty(0))`). Their data was converted into a different-layout kernel tensor, so keeping it would double that memory. This covers:
  - unused zero points, e.g. symmetric GPTQ `qzeros` (Conch, CPU, Marlin, Zentorch via `MPLinearKernel._release_unused_zp`; int8 scaled-mm; Quark int8 linear and MoE);
  - KV-cache scale placeholders (`kv_cache.py`, compressed-tensors KV);
  - released weights (XPU W4A8, wNa8o8, dynamic 4-bit, CPU int8, Triton MXFP4 MoE, INC ARK);
  - Humming leftovers larger than 1/256 of the largest converted tensor.
- **Not changed:** `dispatch_cpu_unquantized_gemm` keeps `main`'s fresh `Parameter(empty(0))` on release, since the released weight can be a tied lm_head shared with `embed_tokens`.
- **Readers see the kernel view.**
  - `kernel_parameters(layer)` returns the live params, each object once under its runtime name. `get_live_param` treats retired or empty params as absent. Humming uses both helpers.
  - The Triton MXFP4 MoE wrapper is stored as a plain `<name>_triton` attribute read via `triton_weight()`, so it no longer takes over the param name.
- **Coverage** (whole-tree enumeration of PWAL-reachable sites on `main`, 1786 rows split across the three PRs): 73 delete/rename sites fixed here, plus 36 sites converted together with them (Humming's delete-then-recreate pattern), plus 7 n/a rows inside the changed hunks.

## Validation

- `pre-commit` passes.
- On GB200 (rebased on `main`), the tests of every changed file: `tests/quantization/` (all), `tests/model_executor/test_utils.py`, `model_loader/test_reload.py`, and the kernel/MoE/LoRA/model tests that import changed modules: 1609 passed.
  - Every remaining failure fails identically on `main` in the same image: Int8 cutlass on SM100, Hopper-only Machete/W4A8, gated repos, DeepGEMM UE8M0 `int32` scales on SM100 (`fp8_block_enabled[auto]`, `fp8_pb_wo_checkpoint_setup`), qutlass forward, int4 per-token KV kernel, AutoRound MXFP8 MoE `NotImplementedError`, and `test_kv_scale_reload`.
  - Existing tests that asserted a deleted or renamed param now assert it is still registered (renames alias the runtime name; Humming leaves the large unused checkpoint weights empty).
  - `test_keep_param_objects.py` runs ModelOpt and compressed-tensors NVFP4 linear and MoE with Marlin and Humming forced; `test_utils.py` covers aliasing, retiring, and the runtime name.
- End-to-end on GB200 (before the rebase), `main` vs the stack with this PR. Each run is a cold start with GSM8K (1319 questions, 5-shot), greedy decoding, a byte digest of every post-PWAL tensor, and an object census of loader-visible params:

  | Config | GSM8K main / stack | Post-PWAL tensors | Loader params registered (main → stack) | Kept with empty storage |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | ModelOpt NVFP4 (Qwen3-30B-A3B) | 0.8878 / 0.8886 | identical | 69% → 100% | 0 |
  | ... forced Marlin (3 runs each) | 0.8749, 0.8901, 0.8863 / 0.8779, 0.8893, 0.8855 | identical | 62% → 100% | 0 |
  | ... forced Humming (3 runs each) | 0.8802, 0.8901, 0.8870 / 0.8734, 0.8863, 0.8961 | identical | 69% → 100% | 0 |
  | compressed-tensors NVFP4, forced Humming | 0.8931 / 0.8946 | identical | 36% → 100% | 0 |
  | compressed-tensors MXFP4 MoE (CUTLASS, `*_weight_packed` → `*_weight`) | 0.8582 / 0.8582 (1314/1319 identical text) | identical | 46% → 100% | 0 |

  - Marlin and Humming are not run-to-run deterministic. Two `main` runs agree on about 390 of 1319 GSM8K outputs, so their rows show three runs per arm.
  - The extra tensors in the stack are aliases, with no extra memory, or kept scalars and per-tensor scales. Kept data adds at most 0.15 MiB per model (under 0.001%).
- Direct load of W1 into the live params (`model.load_weights`, no PWAL): every checkpoint name now resolves.
  - On `main`, ModelOpt NVFP4 with Marlin or Humming fails with `has no parameter 'w2_input_scale'`, and compressed-tensors MXFP4 MoE fails with `has no parameter 'w2_weight_packed'`.
  - With this stack, compressed-tensors MXFP4 MoE loads all 675 tensors with no param moved. ModelOpt NVFP4 then stops at a shape mismatch, because Marlin/Humming repack to a different layout.
  - Direct load is only exact for layout-preserving PWAL, as on `main`; layerwise reload is the supported path.
- Layerwise reload W0 → W1:
  - ModelOpt NVFP4: all tensors are byte-identical to a cold start on W1, and greedy matches `main` 8/8.
  - compressed-tensors MXFP4 MoE: all tensors are byte-identical to a cold start on W1, and greedy matches 8/8.
- Earlier runs of the stack (#62326) gave `tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py`: 74 passed, 1 failed (`test_kv_scale_reload`), the same as on `main`.

## Details

- **Reload:** layerwise reload restores checkpoint-format params before loading. It goes through `layer._parameters`, so both alias names are restored, and a param kept empty is never handed to a `weight_loader`.
- **Humming:** used to delete every param and re-create the set it needs. It now writes through `replace_parameter`. Leftovers are skipped if they alias a replaced param, retired if small, and emptied if large.
- **Weight-only NVFP4 MoE input scales:** Humming's MoE quant config reads the input scales from the layer, so they are retired rather than left live. A live loaded scale would switch Humming to the static checkpoint scale, while `main` uses none.
- **Known limitation:** an aliased param appears under both names in `state_dict()`, so the UVA offloader and elastic-EP scale-up copy it twice (no data change).
- **Not kept (exceptions, listed in #62326):** the online FP8 requantization-source `weight_scale`, AutoGPTQ placeholder MoE biases, and torchao tensor subclasses.

## Update: loaded storage is never shrunk, emptied or split (0dcd74c070..682db58ae5)

A loader-visible param now keeps the checkpoint bytes it had at `create_weights` after PWAL. Its storage is never emptied. When two names refer to the same bytes, they are registered as one Parameter object. This supersedes the "kept with empty storage" item above for every site that has a plain tensor to back.

- **Shrink.** `replace_parameter` copies a smaller result into a prefix view of the param's own storage instead of rebinding it to a new, smaller allocation. Results of equal or larger size are still rebound. Online quantization (`uses_meta_device`) still frees its bf16 source. This covers:
  - ModelOpt/Quark NVFP4 MoE `w13_weight_scale_2` / `w13_input_scale` (`[E,2]` → `[E]`);
  - merged per-tensor scales (`[3]` → `[1]` or scalar: Humming NVFP4 `weight_scale_2`, CT NVFP4 `weight_global_scale` / `input_global_scale`, FP8 `input_scale.max()`);
  - the CUTLASS W4A8 FP8 scales and the CPU AWQ repack, which now go through `replace_parameter`.
- **Triton MXFP4 MoE.** The weights and scales are no longer emptied. Each param holds the swizzled storage, and its `triton_kernels` tensor points at it, so no second copy is kept.
- **Humming.** A converted tensor under a new name is registered as the leftover loaded param it came from (`move_parameter`). This applies when the tensor lives in that param's storage or replaces a large leftover; other leftovers are retired with their data.
  - This removes the second Parameter object that block-FP8 MoE `w13/w2_weight_scale` and NVFP4 `input_scale_2` had over `*_weight_scale_inv` / `input_global_scale`.
  - It also removes the emptied CT WNA16 `*_weight_packed`.
- **No more emptied loaded params.**
  - Unused zero points (Marlin, Conch, CPU, Zentorch), dynamic 4-bit scales and INC ARK qzeros/scales are retired with their data.
  - Zentorch, the DeepSeek-V4 CPU `wo_a` pack, CT W4A8 int8 MoE and CT WNA8O8 put the repacked tensor into the loaded param's storage. The K3 gfx942 MXFP4 repack no longer empties its source.
- **Not changed (reported):** sites whose kernel copy is opaque or split across several tensors still release the loaded weight. Keeping it would double weight memory:
  - CPU oneDNN int8 (`scaled_mm/cpu.py`) and `dispatch_cpu_unquantized_gemm`;
  - AMX MLA `kv_b_proj`;
  - the SM12x b12x linear/MoE/Q8_0 packs.
- **Coverage:** whole-tree AST call-graph enumeration from every PWAL root (1715 site rows), cross-checked with a `git grep` for release and alias patterns.
  - 1030 rows are not applicable: creation time, or not a loader param.
  - 409 `replace_parameter` rows are covered by the shrink rule.
  - The remaining rows were reviewed by hand. The `.data` rebinds there keep the same or a larger size, except the two converted above.

**Census on GB200** (verify-generic-restore census: C1 = storage ≥ checkpoint bytes, C2 = another param or buffer overlapping the bytes). Before = a693c5e9a2; after = 682db58ae5. 4-layer slices; gpt-oss-20b full.

| config | C1 before → after | C2 before → after |
|---|---|---|
| ModelOpt NVFP4 MoE default / FI-CUTLASS / CuteDSL / vLLM CUTLASS | 8 → 0 each | 0 → 0 |
| ModelOpt NVFP4 Marlin / Humming | 4 / 8 → 0 | 0 → 0 |
| CT NVFP4 default / Marlin | 8 → 0 | 12 → 12 (KV-scale buffer views, harmless) |
| CT NVFP4 Humming (new) | – → 0 | – → 12 (same KV-scale views) |
| gpt-oss Triton MXFP4 | 96 → 0 | 0 → 0 |
| Qwen3-30B block-FP8 Humming | 0 → 0 | 8 → 0 |
| controls: q30-fp8 default/Marlin, gpt-oss default | 0 → 0 | 0 → 0 |

In every config, all loader params are still registered as the same object (`missing=0`), and generation works.

- **Tests (GB200):** `model_executor/test_utils.py`, `quantization/test_keep_param_objects.py` (now also asserts storage ≥ loaded bytes and no two param objects on one storage), `test_moe_wna16`, `test_zen_da8w4`, `test_gpt_oss_triton_kernels`, `test_gfx942_int4`, `test_auto_round`, `test_cpu_wna16`, `test_triton_w4a16`, `test_cutlass_w4a16`, `test_reload`, and the MXFP4 / scaled-mm kernel selection tests.
  - 299 passed.
  - 10 failed, and each fails identically on `main`: Hopper-only Machete, AutoRound MXFP8 MoE, and `test_kv_scale_reload`.
  - `pre-commit` passes.
- **Greedy GSM8K, 5-shot completion:**
  - ModelOpt NVFP4 Qwen3-30B-A3B, default backend, 300 questions: this change vs a32836e18b agrees on 245–256/300 outputs, the same as run-to-run (262/300). Accuracy is 0.927 / 0.930 vs 0.923.

title: [RL][Model Loader] Direct weight reload: write checkpoint tensors into the live model
[Model Loader] Refill weight-derived tensors in place on every post-load rerun
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Keep tensors derived from weights (kernel constants, inverse scales, decode copies) at their startup addresses when post-load processing reruns on a weight reload, so captured CUDA graphs read the new values instead of freed memory. Part of the direct weight reload work (RFC #54477, rule 3). Builds on #64357 (merged); replaces aoshen02/vllm#180.

> **Direct reload.** #64336 (direct reload core) is now in main, and this branch has main merged. The direct reload tests that waited on it are back in this PR (see Validation). Results marked "direct" were measured with #64336 on both arms, before it merged.

## Claims

- After a weight reload with CUDA graphs on, MoE models whose post-load step derives kernel tensors serve the same output as before the reload. Without this PR they collapse:
  - gpt-oss-20b (TRT-LLM MXFP4, direct reload): GSM8K 0.39 → 0.01;
  - Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4 (CuteDSL): 0.90 → 0.01 with direct reload, 0.93 → 0.00 with layerwise reload.
- With direct reload (#64336), every tensor the MoE kernel reads keeps its cold-start address across a reload on these backends: TRT-LLM MXFP4/NVFP4, CuteDSL NVFP4 (including per-locality-domain shards), FlashInfer CUTLASS NVFP4/FP8, and per-tensor FP8 (including TRT-LLM FP8 per-tensor's shuffled weights).
- After a draft-model weight update, the tensors the V2 speculator's FULL CUDA graph reads (DFlash/DSpark context K/V weights and norms, including Beam's DFlash2 and Kimi-K3's DSpark drafters) keep their addresses. Without this PR, Beam DFlash2 acceptance fell from 7.03 to 4.89 after an update.
- The same holds for linear kernels that derive tensors in their post-load step (CUTLASS/Triton INT8 asymmetric `azp_adj`, CUTLASS W4A8, Marlin W4A8-INT8/FP8, b12x NVFP4 W4A16, ModelOpt block-quant), for the ROCm gpt-oss MXFP4 AITER shuffles, Kimi-K3 AMD `_w_fold` and the bf16x3 router split, and for MXFP4 MoE on Marlin (gpt-oss-20b GSM8K 0.43 → 0.00 after a reload without this PR, 0.45 → 0.43 with it).
- Humming MoE: its post-load step runs once per quant method; direct reload refuses it (in main with #64336).
- Across 17 served models with direct reload (3 full-checkpoint updates each, measured by aoshen02), GSM8K holds after every update with this PR; on main it collapses on 8 of them (e.g. gpt-oss-120b 0.80 → 0.006, Kimi-K3 0.95 → 0.25).
- No cold-start change: GSM8K, throughput and KV cache match the base on 12 model/backend configurations, all within noise.

## Validation

All runs are on GB200 with nightly `4b47db922` plus this branch's Python files. "Base" = main `255431b5e` + #64357 + #64336.

**Reload with CUDA graphs on.** Start a server on a checkpoint, then record greedy tokens and top-1 logprobs on 8 fixed prompts (one request at a time) and a 300-question GSM8K slice. Push 2 weight updates through the NCCL weight-transfer engine and record the same again. "Greedy = fresh" compares with a fresh server on the last checkpoint sent; for a same-weight update the fresh server is the one before the update.

| Model, MoE backend, reload mode | Update | Base: GSM8K pre → post, greedy = fresh | This PR: GSM8K pre → post, greedy = fresh |
|---|---|---|---|
| gpt-oss-20b, TRT-LLM MXFP4, direct | same weights ×2 | 0.390 → **0.013**, 0/8 | 0.393 → 0.413, **8/8** |
| gpt-oss-20b, TRT-LLM MXFP4, direct | 2 perturbed variants | → 0.007 (fresh 0.007), **0/8** | → 0.003 (fresh 0.003), **8/8** |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4, CuteDSL, direct | same weights ×2 | 0.903 → **0.007** | 0.927 → 0.900 |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4, CuteDSL, layerwise | same weights ×2 | 0.927 → **0.000** | 0.923 → 0.910 |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 (block), TRT-LLM FP8, direct and layerwise | same weights / perturbed | 8/8 | 8/8 |

- The "this PR" MXFP4/NVFP4 rows ran on `a4a859064`; the FP8 rows ran on this PR's first commit (`deaba72c6`). Since then the FP8 and MXFP4/NVFP4 paths changed only in comments and type annotations, and the direct-reload-only branch of `replace_parameter` moved to #64336.
- The perturbed variants flip the low bits of every FP4/FP8 payload and scale the scales by 2^k. These models score ≈0 themselves, so those rows are judged by token equality with the fresh server.
- One perturbed gpt-oss run (job 41424) gave 0/8 against the fresh server. This was not reproducible: three reruns gave 8/8.
- **NVFP4 CuteDSL** is not bit-reproducible across servers: two cold starts agree on 0–2 of 8 greedy sequences. GSM8K is its signal.
- **FP8 block quant** has no per-tensor derived constants, so it is a no-regression row.

**Served reload across models (aoshen02, [review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64692#issuecomment-6543567448)).** Direct reload, GSM8K before → after 3 full-checkpoint updates, main vs this PR plus the review commits (aoshen02/vllm#227, now on this branch). **Fix.**
- `replace_parameter` already refills parameters in place (unchanged here).
- `refill_derived(obj, name, tensor)` (new) refills a plain attribute in place when shape, dtype and device match, else replaces it. It never creates a parameter, and the held tensor must own its storage.

- **Untested in CI:** the Gemma4 MTP, DSpark (Muse, Gemma4, Kimi-K3), Beam DFlash2 and LiLiCorr drafter refills (the CI test covers Qwen3 DFlash), the Muse Spark NVIDIA router fold and NVFP4 MoE constants, the Kimi-K3 specialized decode `refresh_weights` (`decode.py`, `dense.py`, `kda/prepared.py`; validated end to end above) and the ROCm fixes (validated on MI355X above). Muse Spark is the only served row not rerun on the final code (the gated checkpoint is no longer accessible); it passed on the tree before the final simplification commit.

*Found in review, also on main ([aoshen02](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64692#issuecomment-6550731296)):*
- **Compressed-tensors static per-tensor FP8 MoE** fails the first update with `input_scales of w1 and w3 of a layer must be equal`: the loader compares against the post-processed cold-start value. Dropping the check is #64418 L4.

title: [Model Loader] Direct reload: lay the checkpoint out where a relocated weight now starts
body:
## Purpose

With `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, a weight that post-load processing moves into another storage at an offset is reloaded into the wrong place.

`record_checkpoint_layout` records each weight's `storage_offset` before post-load processing. On a reload, `begin_direct_reload` views the weight back to that layout in the storage the weight lives in **now**. If post-load processing moved the weight into a different storage (e.g. `set_` into a fused buffer), the recorded offset belongs to the old storage. The new checkpoint is then written over the neighbouring weight, and the moved weight itself keeps its old bytes.

Example: on ROCm, `prepare_compressor_gemm_fusion` in DeepSeek-V4 does `indexer_weight.set_(fused_weight[main_size:])`. On a reload, the indexer compressor weight was written over the main compressor rows. DeepSeek-V4-Pro GSM8K after reloading the original weights dropped from 0.96 to 0.885.

## Fix

Also record the storage's `data_ptr`. If the weight's storage has changed by reload time, use its current `storage_offset()` instead of the recorded one. Only `reload/direct.py` changes (+4/−1).

## Test Plan

- New `test_reload_into_weight_moved_to_an_offset`. The toy model's post-load processing moves `proj.weight` into a new buffer at an offset. A reload must match a fresh cold start and keep every address.
- `tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_direct_reload.py` on GB300, run with this PR and with main's `direct.py`.
- DeepSeek-V4-Pro (heterogeneous, TP8, CUDA graphs, compressor GEMM fusion on) on MI355X with `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`: cold GSM8K (400, 5-shot), then reload original → perturbed → original, plus a `data_ptr` report. This also needs a separate fix for a `KeyError` in the DeepSeek-V4 ROCm preshuffle scales (stacked on #64692).

title: [Model Loader] Run the model-level post-load hook once at the end of every load and reload
body:
Thanks to Tony Wang (@new-TonyWang) for design and review contributions.

PR 1 of the direct weight reload stack (RFC #54477). It replaces #57733. The code is the same, plus the Llama4 DP-vision fix that #57733 dropped when it was narrowed.

## Problem

RL weight updates do not load a model in one `load_weights` call. The weight-transfer engines (NCCL, IPC, M2N, sharded RDT) and `reload_weights` call it once per bucket, or once per tensor, between `initialize_layerwise_reload` and `finalize_layerwise_reload`. On main, three things go wrong with that:

1. **The model-level hook never runs after a reload.** `finalize_layerwise_reload` only finishes the layers. The model's `process_weights_after_loading()` runs only from the cold-load path. So any state a model derives from its weights in that hook, such as fused buffers or broadcast copies, keeps the old weights' values after an update.
2. **Some models do that work inside `load_weights` instead.** It then runs once per bucket, on partial weights. Under layerwise reload it runs while the layers are still on meta, which fails with `Cannot copy out of meta tensor`. This affects DeepSeek-V4/V4.1, the DFlash/DSpark drafters and Muse Spark.
3. **Checks on "what this call loaded" fire on every bucket.** A bucket that happens not to contain a layer or head raises "MTP layer N weights missing", or silently sets the DSpark `confidence_head` to `None`.

## Fix

- **One finish step.** New `finalize_model_weights(model)` calls the model's `process_weights_after_loading()`. It is called once at the end of a cold load (as before, after per-layer quant processing) and once at the end of every `finalize_layerwise_reload`. That covers `reload_weights` and the NCCL, IPC, M2N and sharded-RDT engines.
  - The sparse NCCL engine patches weights in place without layerwise reload; its `finish_weight_update` now calls `finalize_model_weights` once.
  - An M2N update whose plan is all direct does not call `finalize_layerwise_reload`, so it still skips the hook, as on main.
  - The torchao reload decorator and the expert-substitution error path finish the layers in the middle of a load. They now call `finalize_layerwise_processing`, so they do not run the model hook early.
- **Post-load work moves from `load_weights` into the hook.** Each `load_weights` below now only loads, and the hook runs at the end:
  - DeepSeek-V4 NVIDIA, V4.1 NVIDIA/AMD: the mHC broadcast (V4.1 AMD's `finalize_mega_moe_weights` is a no-op).
  - DeepSeek-V4.1 NVIDIA: the Engram checkpoint page-cache drop and THP collapse. They now also run after every reload and after dummy loads; both are harmless to repeat.
  - DeepSeek-V4 XPU target, MTP and DSpark: `finalize_mega_moe_weights`. The lazy call in MegaMoE `forward()` is removed, since dummy loads run the hook too.
  - Qwen3 DFlash / Qwen3 DSpark / Gemma4 DSpark / Muse Spark DSpark: `_build_fused_kv_buffers`.
    - The hook now runs after quant processing.
    - In Qwen3 DFlash/DSpark and Gemma4 DSpark, the fused path that reads `.weight` directly is used only when the projections are unquantized and not CPU-repacked (`_reads_raw_weights`). Otherwise each projection runs through its quant method.
    - Muse Spark DSpark still slices `qkv_proj.weight` directly, now after quant processing, so a quantized or CPU-repacked Muse Spark drafter would read kernel-layout weights.
    - Qwen3 DFlash's MXFP8 context K/V projection copied the K/V rows of each layer's QKV weight and scales, which is only valid before quant processing. It is now created at construction and loaded from the checkpoint's K/V tensors as they stream through `load_weights`, so its own post-load step runs and a reload refills it in place.
  - Muse Spark AMD and Muse Spark DSpark: `materialize_residual_path_constants`.
- **The DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 VL wrappers drop their workaround.** They had reordered the weight stream so that the language model's in-`load_weights` finalization saw all its weights (`stream_language_model_first`, `finalizes_weights_during_load`, `_weights_finalized`). That is no longer needed and is removed.
- **"Complete load" checks are gated on `is_mtp_completeness_check_enabled()`**, which the weight-transfer engines turn off during an update:
  - The MTP layer checks in DeepSeek-V3.2 AMD, GLM5-next and Kimi-K3 (AMD/NVIDIA).
  - The DSpark `confidence_head` drop in Qwen3, Gemma4 and DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 (NVIDIA/AMD).
  - The Qwen3 DSpark vocab checks.
  - `AutoWeightsLoader._check_skipped_aliases`.
- **dots3 vision: the block compile runs once.** The vision hook now reruns after every reload, and main's `compile_block_modules` would wrap the blocks in another `torch.compile` each time. It now compiles in place with `Module.compile` (parameter names keep no `_orig_mod`) and only once. The vision MoE is unchanged from main: its hook fuses the experts into FP8 once, deletes the checkpoint experts and returns early afterwards, so a reload leaves the vision experts as they are.
- **Llama4 DP vision (`mm_encoder_tp_mode="data"`).**
  - Before: the vision attention used `ReplicatedLinear`, and `load_weights` gathered `q_proj`/`k_proj`/`v_proj` and called `torch.cat` once all three had arrived. An update that sends them in separate calls failed on `torch.cat` of `None`.
  - Now: it uses `QKVParallelLinear` / `RowParallelLinear` with `disable_tp=True` in DP mode, so q/k/v go through the normal stacked mapping and each part is written into its rows as it arrives. `_consolidate_qkv_weights` is removed.
- **Raw Tensorizer loads use the shared loader path.** Loading a non-vLLM-tensorized checkpoint used its own `_load_model_serialized_cpu`, which ran the model hook but skipped per-layer `process_weights_after_loading`. It now goes through `BaseModelLoader.load_model`.

## Not in this PR

- **Weights combined from several checkpoint tensors inside `load_weights`.** A weight plus its scale, or a fused FP8 qkv, still need every part in the same call, as on main:
  - the FP8 indexer `wk` dequant;
  - GLM5-next MLA projections;
  - MiMo-V2 fused qkv;
  - Molmo/Molmo2 split embedding.

  These are later PRs in the stack (PR 6).
- **Drafters that still finish inside `load_weights`, unchanged from main:**
  - LiLiCorr: the coverage check and `materialize_inference_buffers`.
  - Laguna DFlash: the fused KV build.
  - Qwen3 XPress: the `mix.L` check, `fold_from_raw_` and the fused buffers. It also inherits the new DFlash hook, so at cold start its fused KV buffers are built twice, the second time after quant processing.

  A bucketed update of these drafters behaves as on main. LiLiCorr and Laguna are in the F9 follow-up.
- **Hooks that are not safe to rerun.** Every model-level hook reachable from a top-level model was checked for a second run on reloaded weights. These are not fixed here:
  - **DeepSeek-V4 on ROCm (model, MTP, DSpark): a reload now fails instead of leaving wrong weights.**
    - On main this hook ran only at cold start, so a reload left the mega-MoE experts and the preshuffled attention and gate/up weights unshuffled or stale.
    - With this PR it reruns at the end of a reload. With `fuse_shared_expert`, the first run sets `shared_experts = None` (`finalize_mega_moe_weights`), so the second run raises `AttributeError` in `load_shared_expert`.
    - Without it, the mega-MoE `finalize_weights` returns early (stale experts), and `prepare_attn_preshuffle` / `prepare_gateup_preshuffle` shuffle in place again, so layers that the update did not resend are shuffled twice.
  - **dots3 vision MoE: stale, as on main.** Making it reloadable without keeping the BF16 experts resident (about 11 GiB per GPU on dots3-note-prev-fp8 TP4) needs a loader that quantizes each expert into the fused FP8 buffers as it arrives; that is a follow-up.
  - **Muse Spark NVIDIA: stale, as on main.** The router multiplier is folded once and then dropped, and the mega-MoE `finalize_weights` returns early after dropping `w13_weight`.
  - **DeepSeek-V4 XPU mega-MoE: guarded, as on main.** `finalize_weights` returns early once the weights are transformed. The XPU runtime currently rejects mega-MoE, so the hook is a no-op.
  - **Rebuilt as new tensors.** Kimi-K3 AMD's MLA `_w_fold` and Muse Spark's residual `alpha`/`beta` are re-created by the hook, so a captured CUDA graph keeps reading the old ones.
    - On main Kimi-K3's hook did not run on reload, and Muse Spark rebuilt them the same way from `load_weights`, so neither is worse than main.
    - The DFlash/DSpark (Qwen3, Gemma4, Muse Spark) and Beam DFlash2 context K/V buffers, and Kimi-K3 NVIDIA DSpark's `_context_kv_norm_weights`, are also re-created. The V2 speculator's FULL CUDA graph reads the context K/V buffers, so after a reload it reads freed memory and draft acceptance drops (Beam DFlash2 TP4, split reload: 7.03 → 4.89; MiniMax-M3.1 MXFP8 DSpark TP4: 5.70 → 4.07). Outputs stay correct because the target verifies the drafts. Writing these buffers back in place is PR 5 (`refill_derived`); with it, acceptance after the reload matches the cold start.

## Tests

- Unit tests:
  - `tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py::TestModelHookOnSplitLoad`: the model hook runs once, after all weights, for a layerwise reload split into two buckets, a partial layerwise update, and a sparse NCCL update in two chunks.

title: [Model Loader] One post-load hook signature; the loader runs every module's hook
body:
## Purpose

This PR now carries a follow-up to #64357. The earlier revision ran the model-level hook on every load and reload; that landed in reworked form as #64357. Part of RFC #54477.

#64357 made `finalize_model_weights(model)` run once after every full load and reload, but it calls only the **root model's** `process_weights_after_loading`. Module-level hooks still had two signatures:

| module | signature | who called it |
|---|---|---|
| attention layers (`Attention`, `MLAAttention`, `MMEncoderAttention`, Kimi-K3 MLA / KDA, DeepSeek-V4 CPU attention) | `(act_dtype)` | loader, attention pass |
| root model | `()` | `finalize_model_weights` |
| any other module (VL language models, HY-V4 inner model, Dots3 vision MoE FFN, Kimi-K3 AMD MLA wrapper) | `()` | **its parent, by hand** |

So parents forwarded the hook to their submodules by hand: VL wrappers to `language_model`, Kimi-K3 AMD through a `modules()` loop, Dots3 to `visual` and then to each `block.mlp`, and so on. When a parent forgot to forward, the submodule was never processed, with no error. The loader also carried `TODO(lucas): see if there is a way to unify the signatures`.

## Changes

1. **One signature.** Attention layers record `self.act_dtype` at init and take no argument. This is the default dtype the loader sets from `model_config.dtype` while building the model, which is the same value the loader used to pass. Backend impls (`AttentionImpl.process_weights_after_loading(act_dtype)`) are unchanged.
2. **One dispatcher.** After the quant-method pass and the attention pass, `finalize_model_weights` runs the hook of every module, each module after all of its submodules (depth-first; a submodule shared by several parents runs once, before all of them). It skips quant methods (some are `CustomOp` modules whose hook takes `layer`), does not enter quantized layers (their submodules, such as compressed-tensors Hadamard transforms, belong to the quant method and are processed in the per-layer pass), and skips attention layers, which have already run. The stages stay as they are: per-layer quant pass → attention pass → module hooks; later passes may read what earlier ones produced (e.g. MLA absorbs `kv_b_proj` through its transforms in the attention pass).
3. **No hand forwarding.** These are deleted:
   - the DeepSeek-V4 / V4.1 (AMD, NVIDIA) VL wrapper and Kimi-K3 AMD wrapper forwards to `language_model`;
   - the HY-V4 AMD forward to `self.model`;
   - the Dots3 forwards to `visual` and to the `block.mlp` loop;
   - the Kimi-K3 AMD MLA-wrapper loop.

### Behavior

- **Ordering.** As before, all attention layers run before any module hook, and a module's hook runs after its submodules', which is what the deleted forwards guaranteed. Siblings run in registration order. No hook reads a sibling's derived state.
- **No hook runs for the first time, and none runs twice.** I enumerated every class with a no-argument `process_weights_after_loading` (AST scan of `vllm/`). Each one was already reached, either as a root model or through one of the forwards deleted above.
- **Layerwise reload and the sparse NCCL engine** both go through `finalize_model_weights`, so they get the same dispatch.

## Test Plan

- **New test.** `test_finalize_runs_every_module_hook_after_its_submodules` (`tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py`) checks that each module runs exactly once (including one shared by two parents), after its submodules, with quant-method modules, quantized layers' submodules and attention layers skipped. `test_attention_post_load_reads_normalized_transform` runs the real loader `process_weights_after_loading` with a real `CompressedTensorsLinearTransformMethod` + `HadamardTransform` and checks that the attention pass sees the transform already normalized, and normalized once.
- **Updated tests.**
  - The fake attention layers in `test_reload.py`, plus `test_mla_backends`, `test_vit_fp8_scaling` and `test_mla_attn_quant_fusion`, now call the hook without an argument.
  - `test_deepseek_v4_vl` now goes through `finalize_model_weights`.
  - `test_root_model_builds_the_fold` asserted the old forward-by-hand contract, so it is deleted.
- **End to end.** GSM8K before and after weight updates, on GB300.

## Test Result

All runs are on GB300, using the same image and seed, against plain main at `7fc467825d`, the PR's base.

**GSM8K.** Each run measures GSM8K at cold start, then again after 3 full-checkpoint direct reloads (`VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`).

| model | what it exercises | main: cold → after reload | PR: cold → after reload |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-8B | `Attention` reads `act_dtype` from init | 0.895 → 0.895 | 0.895 → 0.895 |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (TP2) | VL wrapper no longer forwards to `language_model` | 0.899 → 0.898 | 0.900 → 0.907 |
| gpt-oss-20b | attention sinks, MXFP4 MoE quant method is a `CustomOp` | 0.438 → 0.023 | 0.444 → 0.022 |

Cold start matches main within noise for all three models. gpt-oss-20b also collapses after a direct reload on plain main; that is a separate issue, fixed in #64692, and unchanged by this PR.

**Unit tests.** 332 passed, 21 failed, 41 skipped. The two new tests pass, and so do the updated tests. `test_attention_post_load_reads_normalized_transform` fails on the previous head of this PR (`fb3b81ad63`, attention saw `1.0` instead of `0.5`), which is the regression a review caught: that head ran Hadamard transforms in the module pass, after MLA had already absorbed `kv_b_proj`. None of the 21 failures comes from this PR:
- **7 DeepSeek-V3 reload tests** (`test_reload_weights` / `test_online_quantize_reload` with DeepSeek-V3-debug, and `test_kv_scale_reload`). They fail the same way on plain main.
- **14 GLM5-next KDA / sequence-parallel tests.** They failed only in the full batch run. Rerun on their own, they pass on both main and this PR.

title: [Model Loader] One finish for every update path; drop refresh_derived_weights
body:
## Overview

Every load and weight-update path now finishes through `finalize_model_weights`, and weight-derived state has one hook again: each module's own `process_weights_after_loading()`.

Before this PR the paths finished differently:

| path | quant methods | attention-like layers | other modules' hooks |
|---|---|---|---|
| cold start, direct reload (`process_weights_after_loading`) | yes | yes (loader pass) | yes |
| layerwise reload | yes (per layer) | yes (`_finalize_attention_layer`) | yes |
| sparse NCCL finish | — | **no** | yes |
| kernel-format `reload_weights` | — | **no** | **no** |

#64886 covered the two gaps with a second per-module hook, `refresh_derived_weights()`, and a walker. Kimi-K3 ROCm's KDA layer is a `MambaBase`, hence attention-like, so `finalize_model_weights` skipped its hook and its decode copies stayed stale after a sparse update or a kernel-format reload.

This PR closes both gaps without a second hook:

- `finalize_model_weights` runs every module's hook in one children-first traversal, attention-like layers included (those under `device_loading_context` when given a target device). Attention hooks need the quant pass done, which the loader does first, and must precede their ancestors' hooks, which children-first gives; no hook reads attention-derived state from a non-ancestor, so there is no separate attention pass. Quant methods and the submodules of quantized layers are still skipped.
- The loader's own attention pass and the hook call in layerwise `_finalize_attention_layer` are removed, so every hook runs once per load, from one place.
- Sparse NCCL ends with `finalize_model_weights` alone.
- Kernel-format `reload_weights` now ends with `finalize_model_weights` too, under `weights_already_processed()`. DeepSeek-V4 ROCm's model hook skips its preshuffle in that mode.
- `refresh_derived_weights` is removed. The Kimi-K3 ROCm KDA and MLA bodies go back into their `process_weights_after_loading()`, which write in place (`copy_`, `refill_derived`).

With every hook guaranteed to run after every load, dummy loads included, these fallbacks are dead and are removed:

- GLM5-next: the wrapper hook that ran its language model's hook a second time (the language model is a submodule, so it already runs), and the indexer's forward-time "post-load processing never ran" call.
- MoE runner: the forward-time build of the fused router + shared-expert gate.
- Qwen3 DFlash and Muse Spark DSpark: the lazy build of the context KV buffers in `precompute_and_store_context_kv`.
- Kimi-K3 NVIDIA DSpark: the lazy build of its context KV metadata.
- Gemma-4 MTP: the forward-time caching of the full lm_head weight (the hook builds it for TP>1).
- Kimi-K3 ROCm KDA: the `is_weights_pre_processed()` early return. The hook only copies `conv1d.weight` and `o_norm.weight`, which stay in place, so it is valid for pre-processed weights too.

Two hooks are fixed so that they can run on every load:

- Laguna DFlash built its fused context KV inside `load_weights` (per call, and never on dummy loads). It now builds it in `process_weights_after_loading`.
- dots3 vision FP8 MoE returned early after the first run and deleted its checkpoint experts, so a reload had nothing to write. It now keeps the experts and refills the fused buffers in place. Cost: the BF16 vision experts stay resident next to the fused FP8 copy.

Not removed: the Kimi-K3 NVIDIA model hook that calls `specialized_decode` (a plain object, not a module) and the Muse Spark MoE runner calling `post_expert_finalize` (submodules of quantized layers are not walked); both still need their explicit calls.

torchao: inside `reload_weights` the torchao reload decorator is already off. A direct `model.load_weights` reload of a torchao model no longer runs attention hooks. Its removal is proposed in #65913.

Kernel-format weights are not post-processed again, because quant methods do not rerun. As on the sparse path and the weight-cache loader, module and attention hooks must rebuild state from the current weights instead of transforming the weights in place. Direct reload already reruns these same hooks on every update.

Side effect on sparse NCCL: attention hooks now run after a sparse update, so state they derive (for example MLA's `W_UK`/`W_UV` from `kv_b_proj`) is rebuilt as well. Layerwise reload is unchanged apart from where the attention hooks are called from.

## Validation

MI355X (gfx950), image `vllm-rocm` nightly `3966924d` with this branch's `vllm/` and `tests/` over the installed package, head `8c7b43e05c` (job 33373):

- `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_decode.py`, `test_amd_qb_uk_fold.py`, `tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py`: 137 passed, 17 skipped, 1 xpassed, 2 failed. The 2 failures are the NVFP4A16 `DeepSeek-V3-debug` cases of `test_reload_weights`, which fail on the base on this ROCm image too (as in #64886).
- Before the attention change (walker removed, kernel-format reload calling `finalize_model_weights`), `test_decode_weights_staged_after_loading[*-float32]` failed: the KDA hook was skipped as an attention-like layer.

NVIDIA A/B, main `831dd92674` vs head `8c7b43e05c` (GSM8K pre vs post, sleep mode, 3 updates, direct and layerwise, throughput before and after):

- No failure is specific to this PR on GLM-5.3-Flash, Nemotron-3.5, Qwen3.5 (fused gate), Qwen3 DFlash, Laguna DFlash, DSv4.1-Flash, Gemma-4 MTP, Muse Spark + DSpark, dots3, Kimi-K3 + DSpark. Throughput is level between arms.
- Fixed by this PR: dots3 direct and layerwise (0.9621→0.9515, 0.9538→0.9545; main fails on `visual.blocks.*.mlp.experts`), Laguna DFlash layerwise (main fails on meta tensors).
- Fail the same on both arms: Kimi-K3 + DSpark direct (illegal memory access after updates), layerwise OOM on Kimi-K3, DSv4.1 and Muse Spark.
- DSv4.1, Gemma-4 and Muse Spark ran with level 1 sleep, because level 2 discards weights the update does not send.

AMD MI350X (gfx950) at `145fb8c684`, sleep level 2 on every update, GSM8K on the first 400 questions:

- Unit tests (job 8289): 140 passed, 2 failed, 17 skipped, 1 xpassed. The 2 failures are the NVFP4A16 `DeepSeek-V3-debug` cases, which also fail on main.
- DeepSeek-V4-Flash AITER=1 (job 8286): direct 0.9700→0.9575, kernel-format 0.9550 / 0.9575 / 0.9550, layerwise 0.9650→0.9575. Throughput 1635→1858 tok/s.
- DeepSeek-V4-Flash AITER=0 (job 8287): direct 0.9625→0.9625, kernel-format 0.9650 / 0.9550 / 0.9625. Throughput 823→828 tok/s.
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash AITER=1, TP4: direct 0.9000→0.9050 (job 8332), kernel-format 0.8975 / 0.0225 (perturbed) / 0.9025 (job 8357).

The kernel-format regression seen at `8c7b43e05c` (DeepSeek-V4 AITER=1, GSM8K 0.0075, double preshuffle) is fixed by `f81b1a7764`.

Same on main, not caused by this PR: DeepSeek-V4 AITER=0 layerwise fails with `too many resources requested for launch`; `_dsv4_wo_a_bf16` is not refreshed (aoshen02/vllm#235).

Open on AMD: DeepSeek-V4.1 layerwise is not attributed (GSM8K 0 with HTTP 400 on main and on `f81b1a7764`, with incomplete runs). One Kimi direct run (job 8288) hung for 30 minutes in an extra update without sleep, with no server error, and did not reproduce in two reruns. DeepSeek-V4 updates ran at TP1 only. title: [Bugfix][ROCm][Kimi-K3] Refresh derived weight copies after in-place weight writes
body:
## Overview

This adds an opt-in module hook, `refresh_derived_weights()`, plus a walker in `weight_utils.py`. The walker is called from three shared paths that overwrite `state_dict()` tensors in place without the per-layer post-load hook:
- `SparseNCCLWeightTransferEngine.finish_weight_update`;
- the kernel-format branch of `reload_weights`;
- `ElasticEPScalingExecutor.prepare_new_worker`.

It does nothing unless a module defines the hook. Today only the Kimi-K3 ROCm KDA layer and MLA wrapper do, and the elastic-EP call has no model that reaches it yet. The PR also makes the Kimi-K3 ROCm `_w_fold` rebuild write in place.

Kimi-K3 on ROCm derives three tensors from its weights and keeps them outside `state_dict()`:
- `decode_conv1d_weight`, read by the AITER Gluon and HIP fused decode kernels;
- `decode_norm_weight`, read by the HIP kernel only;
- `_w_fold`, a plain attribute read by the fused decode-query GEMM.

The KDA copies (the first two) go stale on all three paths. `_w_fold` goes stale on the kernel-format reload and on elastic EP. On sparse NCCL it is rebuilt, but as a new tensor that CUDA graphs captured earlier do not read.

Related (all merged):
- #60110 added `_w_fold`.
- #61207 stages the KDA copies at load.
- #64158 builds `_w_fold` from the root model's hook.
- #64357 runs the model-level hook after every load, checkpoint-format reload and sparse NCCL update, but not after a kernel-format reload.

## Claims

The kernel-format reload claim is covered by the updated unit test. The sparse NCCL, elastic-EP and `_w_fold` claims come from reading the code (see Validation).

- **Kernel-format `reload_weights(..., is_checkpoint_format=False)`:** the Kimi-K3 ROCm KDA decode copies are re-staged from the reloaded weights, at the same addresses. On main they keep the values staged at load, while prefill reads the reloaded weights.
- **Sparse NCCL weight updates:** the same holds for an update that writes `conv1d.weight` or `o_norm.weight`.
- **Elastic-EP scale-up:** new ranks re-derive these tensors from the weights received from their peer, instead of keeping values computed from the dummy load. This is defensive for Kimi-K3. It does not set `num_moe_layers`, so EPLB never registers it and an elastic-EP scale-up cannot complete on it today (it fails at the `model.expert_weights` and `model_states` lookups).
- **`_w_fold`:** rebuilt in place. On main, layerwise reload and sparse NCCL assign a new `_w_fold`, so CUDA graphs captured before the rebuild keep the old, freed tensor's address.
- **Other models:** no change. Only modules that define `refresh_derived_weights()` are called.

## Validation

All runs used one MI355X (gfx950) with image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-3966924d566340e971a6da313e790d05492aa505`, with this branch's `vllm/` and `tests/` over the installed package. The image is 193 commits behind the base 5a233286c6; `csrc/kimi_k3` did not change in between.

`test_decode_weights_staged_after_loading` builds a real `KimiK3DeltaAttention`, then reloads every parameter with new values through `reload_weights(..., is_checkpoint_format=False)`. It checks that the staged copies match the reloaded weights and that no buffer moved.

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_decode.py tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_qb_uk_fold.py` | 45 passed |
| `test_decode_weights_staged_after_loading` on the base (every changed `vllm/` file from main, new test kept) | 2 failed, 2 passed |
| `pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py` | 82 passed, 17 skipped, 1 xpassed, 2 failed. The same 2 fail on the base: the NVFP4A16 `DeepSeek-V3-debug` cases of `test_reload_weights`, whose engine fails to start on this ROCm image. |
| `VLLM_ALLOW_INSECURE_SERIALIZATION=1 pytest tests/distributed/test_weight_transfer.py` (4 GPUs) | 114 passed, 26 skipped, 3 failed. The same 3 fail on the base: the `*_weight_transfer_between_processes` tests, whose Ray actors hit `invalid device ordinal` with two visible GPUs. |

On the base, both fp32-state cases fail after the reload, on `decode_conv1d_weight`. The bf16-state cases allocate no copies.

```
tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_decode.py:446: in test_decode_weights_staged_after_loading
tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_decode.py:424: in check_staged
E   AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not equal!
E   Mismatched elements: 18432 / 18432 (100.0%)
```

`pre-commit run --files <changed files>` (ruff 0.14.0, mypy): clean.

CI: `:amd: (MI355) Kimi K3` runs `pytest -v -s models/kimi_k3 --ignore=models/kimi_k3/test_prefix_cache.py` on this PR. The B200 step skips this ROCm-only file.

Not validated:
- **End to end:** no serving or RL run of Kimi-K3 on any of the three paths.
- **Call sites without a test:** the sparse NCCL and elastic-EP call sites. Both elastic-EP scale-up tests, `tests/distributed/test_elastic_ep.py` and `tests/v1/distributed/test_external_lb_dp.py::test_external_lb_elastic_ep_scale_up`, use DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat, which has no module with the hook.
- **The in-place `_w_fold` rebuild:** no existing Kimi-K3 test builds a real MLA wrapper with `_fold_qb_uk` enabled (AITER MLA, fp8 KV cache, unquantized `q_b_proj`, no DCP or PCP), and adding one is a larger setup than this fix.

## Details

**How it was found.** By reading the code while reviewing #63612. It was not observed in a serving or RL run.

**Root cause.**
- The KDA copies are staged only in the layer's `process_weights_after_loading`. `_w_fold` is built only from the Kimi-K3 model-level hook.
- The kernel-format branch of `reload_weights` copies parameters and runs neither hook.
- Sparse NCCL ends with `finalize_model_weights`, which reaches the MLA wrappers through the model hook but not the KDA layers.
- Elastic EP builds new ranks with `load_dummy_weights=True` (`elastic_execute.py:273`), so both hooks derive these tensors from dummy weights. `batch_transfer_weights` then receives only `model.state_dict()` from a peer (`:97`) and runs no post-load pass.

**Change.**
- **The walker:** `weight_utils.refresh_derived_weights(model)` calls `refresh_derived_weights()` on every module that defines it, under `no_grad`.
- **The hook contract** (in the docstring): idempotent; reads only non-expert `state_dict()` tensors, since elastic EP moves routed experts later; no collectives; writes in place.
- **Callers:**
  - `prepare_new_worker`, after the transfer and `torch.accelerator.synchronize()`, under the worker's vLLM config;
  - `finish_weight_update`, after `finalize_model_weights`;
  - the kernel-format branch of `reload_weights`, after the copy loop.
- **`KimiK3DeltaAttention`:** the existing copy body moves into `refresh_derived_weights()`. `process_weights_after_loading` keeps the IPC weight-cache guard and calls it.
- **`KimiK3MultiHeadLatentAttentionWrapper`:** `process_weights_after_loading()` and `refresh_derived_weights()` both rebuild `_w_fold`, which is copied in place once it exists.
- **Precedent:** `refresh_quantized_lm_heads` (`layers/quantization/online/lm_head.py:157`) re-derives copies in place after a weight reload, for the same CUDA-graph reason.

**Alternatives considered.**
- **Re-stage the KDA copies from the Kimi-K3 model hook (`amd/linear.py:1174`).** Sparse NCCL already runs that hook, so this fixes sparse NCCL with no core change. But the kernel-format reload runs no hook, and the elastic-EP receiver runs none, so a core call is needed anyway.
- **Refresh from the weight loader, as #63612 does for its GLM layer.** This covers writes that go through `load_weights`, such as sparse NCCL. It misses the kernel-format `param.copy_` and the elastic-EP `state_dict()` copy. #61207 also moved Kimi-K3's staging out of the loaders because dummy loads skip them.
- **Register the buffers as persistent, so `state_dict()` carries them.** This covers elastic EP only. It changes the key set of every saved Kimi-K3 `sharded_state` checkpoint ("Missing keys" on load), makes that key set depend on the decode backend picked at runtime, and does not cover `_w_fold`.
- **Re-run `finalize_model_weights` or the per-layer hooks on new elastic ranks.** Model-level hooks are not idempotent on already-processed weights in general: DeepSeek-V4 AMD preshuffles in its hook.

**Trade-offs and limits.**
- On sparse NCCL, `_w_fold` is now built twice per update (model hook, then the walker). That is one extra `_w_fold` build per MLA layer: `kv_b_proj` dequant, an einsum and a concat, then an in-place copy.
- The same pattern is left for follow-ups:
  - the Kimi-K3 NVIDIA KDA buffers, which only the weight loaders fill, so they are uninitialized after a dummy load;
  - `GateLinear._bf16x3_weight` for fp32-router models on gfx950;
  - #63612's GLM-5.3-Flash decode copy, a model that does reach elastic EP. Its layer could implement this hook.

**Duplicate check.**
- I searched open and closed PRs for `refresh_derived_weights`, `decode_conv1d_weight`, `_w_fold` and elastic-EP buffer staleness, and found the PRs listed above.
- #63612 refreshes its own layer's copy from its weight loader. No PR covers kernel-format reloads or elastic EP, or adds a hook that every in-place path calls.

title: [Model Loader] Direct reload: reset MoE expert padding at begin
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

At the start of a direct weight reload (`VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, #64336), zero MoE expert padding, so that post-load processing reruns over the same bytes as a cold start. Part of the direct weight reload work (#54477).

MoE expert parameters are often larger than the checkpoint tensors loaded into them: DeepEP rounds the hidden size up, MXFP4 / TRT-LLM / AITER backends round the intermediate size, and block-aligned FP8 TP pads shards. Loaders copy only the checkpoint part. On a direct reload the padding then holds the previous post-processed bytes, which post-load processing processes again. After a `load_format=dummy` cold start (the usual RL setup) it holds random values.

## Claims

- **gpt-oss-20b (TP2, MXFP4), direct reload through IPC weight transfer:** every tensor is bit-identical to a fresh start, both after 3 same-weight syncs and after a dummy start plus one sync. On main, 168 expert tensors differ after every sync and drift from one sync to the next. After a dummy start, 288 differ and GSM8K drops about 2 points.
- Cold start and layerwise reload are unchanged.
- No loader changes: whether to fill is decided from `moe_config` when the checkpoint layout is recorded at cold start, so it also covers dummy and other cold starts that skip loaders, and the load plan (#64418) that bypasses them.

## Validation

**This PR's head (`1e25cc87e2`) with #66010 (`84ab98b6d8`) applied, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash** (GB200, TP4, `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, 1319 questions, 3 updates; nightly `a2bcb5657a` with Python files overlaid). Differing expert parameters are 0 on every rank after every update. Jobs 45934, 45935.

| Sleep | Start | GSM8K cold → after 1 → after 3 | Differing |
|---|---|---|---|
| Level 2 | Real | 0.9090 → 0.8984 → 0.9007 | 0 / 160 |
| | Dummy | — → 0.8999 → 0.9007 | 0 / 160 |
| None | Real | 0.9007 → 0.8969 → 0.9022 | 0 / 160 |
| | Dummy | — → 0.9060 → 0.9037 | 0 / 160 |

**Layerwise reload (`VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=layerwise`, the default).** `materialize_meta_tensor` now zeroes the tensor it allocates, because loaders write only checkpoint regions and padding otherwise keeps uninitialized memory. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP4, no sleep, 1319 questions, on main `5c97556318` with and without that one line. Jobs 46042, 46043.

| Arm | Differing after updates 1 / 2 / 3 | GSM8K cold → after 1 → after 3 |
|---|---|---|
| main | 160 / 160 / 160 | 0.9037 → 0.0 → 0.0 |
| With the zero fill | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0.8954 → 0.9007 → 0.9030 |

`test_padded_moe_reload_releases_each_layer` fails 8 of 16 cases without the line.

**main vs this PR, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash** (GB200, TP4, `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8`, `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, reload from disk, no sleep mode; nightly `a2bcb5657a` with each arm's Python files overlaid, PR at e6403484fc; later commits change a comment and a CI trigger and merge main). "Differing" counts expert parameters per rank, out of 160, against a real cold start on the same arm. GSM8K is 5-shot greedy over 1319 questions. Jobs 45840, 45841.

| Start | Arm | Differing after updates 1 / 2 / 3 | GSM8K cold → after 1 → after 3 |

| Real | main | 120 / 120 / 120 | 0.9052 → 0.9105 → 0.8984 |

| Dummy | main | 160 / 160 / 160 | — → 0.8787 → 0.8400 |

On main after a dummy start the padding is random and GSM8K keeps falling across updates. Run-to-run noise on the real cold start is up to 1.5 points, so the real-start GSM8K rows don't separate the arms; the tensor counts do.

**End to end** (GB200, nightly wheel 81a2879403 with each arm's Python files overlaid, `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, real IPC weight transfer). - On main, the gpt-oss tensors that differ are expert biases and scales after real-start syncs, and all six expert parameters after a dummy start.
- The two Qwen3 configs are already correct on main: `_zero_intermediate_padding` and the block-aligned TP loader fill rewrite their padding on every load. They show the change does no harm.
- \* Attention KV-cache scales the checkpoint doesn't contain keep their random dummy values. This happens on both arms and isn't MoE padding; it's fixed separately (KV-scale `dummy_weight_value`).
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: on main the 120 tensors per rank are `w13_weight`, `w13_weight_scale` and `w2_weight_scale` of all 40 MoE layers, and their bytes change on every sync; after a dummy start `w2_weight` differs too. PR 3 ran at b5130fff61, main at e5d9bad98e. † The Engram embedding tables (about 203 GB, tensors of ~98 GB) can't be sent through the transfer path, so after a dummy start they keep dummy values in both arms and GSM8K isn't meaningful there; they are the only tensors that differ on this PR.

**Cold-start A/B** (A = main 81a2879403, B = this PR a096f3f138, same nightly wheel, same node, arms back to back). GSM8K 5-shot greedy, 1319 questions; throughput from `vllm bench serve`, random 1024 in / 256 out, concurrency 64.

| Model (GB200, TP) | GSM8K A → B | Output tok/s A → B | KV cache A → B |

| gpt-oss-20b MXFP4, chat GSM8K (TP2) | 0.8886 → 0.8976 | 14390 → 14727 | 7.259M → 7.259M |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B BF16 (TP4; intermediate 192 → 256) | 0.8946 → 0.8893 | 9230 → 9444 | 6.791M → 6.791M |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 block (TP4) | 0.9045 → 0.9083 | 7269 → 7098 | 7.274M → 7.274M |

All within noise: GSM8K within 1 point, throughput within 2.4% in both directions, KV cache identical. At cold start this PR only records the fill list (jobs 44551–44553).

**Unit tests** (GB200, job 44519):
- `tests/kernels/moe/test_fp8_tp_loading.py::test_direct_reload_after_dummy_start_resets_padding[block|static]` builds a real fp8 `RoutedExperts` with intermediate 256 → 384, fills every parameter with 7 instead of loading, records, then begins and loads. It checks that the result equals a zero-initialized load, that per-expert scalars and `e_score_correction_bias` are left alone, and that the record made at cold start decides the fill.
- `test_fp8_tp_loading.py` and `test_direct_reload.py` and `test_moe_weight_loading_padded.py` on the final code: 153 passed (GB200 job 23710). Earlier, `test_gpt_oss_weight_loading.py` and `test_reload.py -k padded` (layerwise) also passed.

## Details

**Design.**
- `RoutedExperts.padding_fill_params()` applies when `moe_config` shows the hidden size or the per-partition intermediate size rounded up past its unpadded value, or block-aligned TP sharding.
- It returns the layer's parameters minus per-expert scalars: a parameter is filled if it has more than two values per expert. So per-tensor and static input scales, which may be absent from the checkpoint, are kept.
- `record_checkpoint_layout` stores `(module, name)` at cold start, before post-load processing. Some post-load processing pads only the runtime copy and writes the padded size back into `moe_config`, so the decision must not be made later.
- `begin_direct_reload` looks up each name after the view-back, skips parameters post-load processing has dropped, and zero-fills the rest whole. Loaders then overwrite every checkpoint region.

**Requirement.** The fill erases the checkpoint region too, so every checkpoint tensor loaded into these parameters must be resent on every update. The direct delivery contract in `direct.py` says so; the completeness check (F2 in #54477) will enforce it.

**Padding value.** Everything is filled with 0. A padding-only scale block only multiplies weights the same fill zeroes, so its value doesn't change the output. MXFP4 (DeepSeek-V4.1, gpt-oss) and NVFP4 scales are created as zeros or empty, so 0 also matches a cold start. Block-aligned TP padding is rewritten by its loader after the fill, with scales at 1. Weights created with `torch.empty` had uninitialised padding at cold start; they get 0 here.

**`moe_config` is the source today, not the only possible one.** A layer padded some other way implements `padding_fill_params()` and reuses the same fill.

**Not changed.** Layerwise reload, the block-aligned TP loader fill, and `_zero_intermediate_padding` (cold start still needs it, since those weights are `torch.empty`).

**History.** This replaces this PR's earlier design, where loaders recorded the padding regions on every load and `fill_padding` wrote them before post-load processing. That design worked with layerwise reload and partial updates. Under the decision to require full updates and to drop layerwise reload (#54477), the fill at begin is much smaller and needs no loader changes. The streamed gpt-oss MXFP4 TP split moved to #65353, and Inkling AMD's padding (#64690) is covered by this fill.

title: [RL] NCCL weight transfer: release cached memory after a weight update
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

After an NCCL weight update, release the unused memory held by torch's caching allocator: one `torch.accelerator.empty_cache()` at the end of `NCCLWeightTransferEngine.finish_weight_update`. Part of the direct weight reload work (RFC #54477); independent of the other PRs.

## Claims

- After every NCCL weight update, the server's torch reserved memory is back to its cold-start level. On Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 (TP=2), each rank has 3.7–4.4 GiB more free device memory after a sync than on main.
- Weights, accuracy, throughput and KV cache size are unchanged.
- Cost: the next update allocates its receive buffers again. Median sync time went from 6.67 s to 7.13 s (+7%, one run per arm).

## Validation

Both setups use GB200 and Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 with the server at TP=2. The trainer runs on other GPUs and sends the weights over NCCL.

**Weight-sync bench.** The [state-transition verifier](https://github.com/hao-aaron/vllm-state-transition-verifier) `run_bench.py` setup:
- trainer `fsdp=2`, `--backend nccl`;
- 1 warmup + 3 measured syncs, each with a perturbed checkpoint;
- server `--max-model-len 2048 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8`;
- every tensor is compared against a fresh server at the end.

Server memory per rank after each sync (all four syncs agree within 2 MiB):

| | allocated | reserved | device free | median sync |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 146.30 GiB | 150.72 GiB | 29.82 GiB | 6.67 s |
| this PR | 146.28 GiB | 146.36 GiB | 34.18 GiB | 7.13 s |

Weights compared with a fresh server: 0 mismatched, 0 moved, in both arms. Both arms also report the same 192 `moe_quant_config._w1/_w2.scale` tensors re-created by layerwise reload; that happens on main and is unrelated to this change.

**A/B after one update.** Main vs this PR on the same nightly wheel, same node, back to back:
- each arm cold starts, receives one NCCL update of the same checkpoint, then is measured;
- GSM8K: 5-shot greedy, all 1319 questions;
- throughput: `vllm bench serve`, random 1024 in / 256 out, concurrency 64;
- server: `--max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8`.

| | GSM8K | output tok/s | KV cache | device free after the sync | torch reserved after the sync |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 0.8954 | 8276 | 2.794M | 31.23 GiB | 147.92 GiB |
| this PR | 0.8946 | 8407 | 2.794M | 34.89 GiB | 144.27 GiB |

- **Noise:** GSM8K differs by one question and throughput by 1.6%. Running the same code as both arms gives ±1 question and 1.8%.
- **Memory:** with this PR, reserved memory after the sync equals its cold-start value. Free memory is 0.62 GiB below cold start, which is the NCCL communicator created during the first sync. On main it is 4.28 GiB below.
- **Why the gain differs from the bench (3.66 vs 4.36 GiB):** this setup uses a different nightly, a different `--max-model-len`, and one sync instead of four.

**CI:** no unit test. The effect only shows up in device memory after a real NCCL update between two processes. The existing NCCL engine tests don't run one, and a mocked test would only assert that the call happens.

## Details

After `finalize_layerwise_reload`, the caching allocator keeps the freed receive buffers and post-load temporaries reserved. Torch can reuse that memory; nothing outside torch can. That includes other processes on the GPU (e.g. a colocated trainer) and allocations that bypass the caching allocator (NCCL, e.g. a newly created communicator).

`empty_cache()` releases the unused cached segments once per update, after all weights are loaded, so the transfer itself is unaffected. Blocks still in use and CUDA graph pools are not touched. `base_loader.py` already calls `empty_cache()` after loading and after post-processing at cold start.

Only the NCCL engine is changed, as that is the path measured here. The other layerwise engines (IPC, M2N, sharded RDT) could get the same call in a follow-up.

title: [Sleep Mode] Level 2 discards only parameters
body:
## Overview

Level 2 frees GPU memory by not keeping what can be rebuilt, and the only thing rebuilt on wake is what the weight update writes: parameters. Today it discards everything allocated while the model was built, because the weights pool wraps model construction. The rest then has to be rescued one site at a time: buffers by name, and everything held some other way is lost. With this change `sleep(level=2)` states what the caller rewrites and keeps the rest, at the same address. Part of the direct weight reload work (#54477, F11).

This replaces this PR's earlier site-by-site fixes (MXFP4 permute cache, DeepSeek-V4.1 `permute_on_load`, GEMM-RS/AR), which are reverted here because the rule covers them.

## Failures this addresses

All come from non-parameter state in the weights pool. Measured on GB200 without any fix:

| State | How it is held | Failure after a level-2 wake |
|---|---|---|
| GEMM-RS/AR peer pointer table from `symm_mem.rendezvous` | Inside the torch handle | Table reads all zeros, then `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` on the first forward. Kimi-K3 placeholder weights, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with GEMM-RS |
| DeepSeek-V4.1 `permute_on_load` indices | Weight loader closure | GSM8K 0.90 → 0.0, and later reloads don't repair it |
| MXFP4 TRT-LLM permute cache | Quant method attribute | gpt-oss-20b GSM8K 0.375 → 0.0 |

The same pattern is in code but not measured: Inkling and Beam peer tables, DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram handles (#64922), plain attributes (#60009), attention impl state (#62634).

## Change

- `CuMemAllocator.sleep` and `XpuMemAllocator.sleep` take `discardable`: a weights allocation is discarded only if every live block in it starts at an address in `discardable`. An address that doesn't match keeps the allocation, so a wrong match costs host memory, not state.
- `Worker.sleep(level=2)` passes the storage addresses of the parameters the update rewrites, through `SleepModeBackend.suspend(discardable)`. That replaces `level`, which said the same thing: nothing discardable is level 1. It changes a plugin interface, so an out-of-tree backend must follow.

Kept tensors stay in `weights` and return on `wake_up(["weights"])`, so tags keep their meaning. Level 1 is unchanged.

## Removed

These existed to survive level 2, which now keeps them:

- Model state in the runtime pool (#63548), LoRA state in the runtime pool (#62358), and the MiniMax-M3 MSA prefill workspace in the runtime pool (#64856). All three are built during `load_model`; none is a parameter.
- The CPU copies of `named_buffers()`, on every platform.
- The separate CPU save and restore of `sleep_preserve_parameter_names`. Preserved parameters are now just not discardable, so their backup goes through the allocator: pinned where `PIN_MEMORY` is on, instead of pageable, and kept across wake for reuse.

Left in place: buffers registered for this reason (they are still correct as buffers), and the KV-init and CUDA graph runtime pools, which are outside `load_model`.

## Not covered

title: [Model Loader] DeepSeek-V4 ROCm: keep the preshuffle scales out of the module's parameters
body:
## Purpose

With `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, DeepSeek-V4 on ROCm crashes on the first reload:

```
KeyError: 'layers.0.attn.fused_wqa_wkv.weight_scale_inv'
KeyError: 'layers.0.ffn.shared_experts.gate_up_proj.weight_scale_inv'
```

`prepare_attn_preshuffle` and `prepare_gateup_preshuffle` store the scale `nn.Parameter` itself as a module attribute (`self._wqa_wkv_scale = ws`, `self._gateup_scale = ws`). `nn.Module.__setattr__` then registers it as a second parameter under that name, which the reload does not know.

## Fix

- Store `ws.detach()`, a plain tensor on the same storage, so nothing new is registered.
- Assign it through `refill_derived`, so a reload refills it in place at the address the captured CUDA graphs read.
- Do the same for the other derived tensors of `_prepare_fp8_wo_a`: `_wo_a_e8m0_scale`, `_wo_a_cos_cache` and `_wo_a_sin_cache`.
- Move the `replace_parameter` / `refill_derived` imports to the top of both files.

## Test Plan

DeepSeek-V4-Pro (heterogeneous, TP8, CUDA graphs, compressor GEMM fusion on) on MI355X with `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`:

1. cold GSM8K (400, 5-shot)
2. reload the original weights
3. reload perturbed weights
4. reload the original weights again

Plus a `data_ptr` report against cold start. This was run together with #65281, which fixes the compressor-fusion offset on reload.

## Test Result

| tree | cold | reload orig | reload perturbed | reload orig | moved tensors |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| #64692 head | 0.9650 | `KeyError: 'layers.0.attn.fused_wqa_wkv.weight_scale_inv'` | – | – | – |

title: [Test][Model Loader] Direct weight reload equals a cold start, bitwise
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

An end-to-end test that a streamed direct weight reload (`VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, #64336) leaves the engine exactly as a cold start would, on every rank, for single-GPU and TP2 / EP / EPLB / DP2 layouts. It adds two B200 CI steps that run it. PR 9 of the direct weight reload stack (#54477). It is the test half of #61287, rewritten for current main; the fixes from #61287 are in PR 10.

## Claims

- **New test `tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload_refit.py`.** An `AsyncLLM` engine cold-starts on checkpoint A with CUDA graphs captured, then reloads B and then A through the worker's weight-update session: `start_weight_update`, the model's own `load_weights` in device-tensor batches of 16, then `finish_weight_update`. The engine runs with the IPC transfer backend configured, so the KV-cache loan, incomplete-update bookkeeping and backend gating run as in RL. After **each** reload it checks, on every worker of every DP engine:
  - **State.** Every tensor and every host scalar the model holds equals the reference: after B, a fresh engine on B started in **layerwise** mode, so the reference shares no direct-mode cold-start code; after A, the cold start on A.
  - **Addresses.** No tensor moved (`data_ptr`, stride, storage offset), because captured graphs read the old addresses. The cold-start storages stay referenced, so a free followed by a reallocation shows as a move.
  - **Memory.** No PyTorch allocator block appeared or was freed. With one chunk in flight, the peak stays within the largest chunk plus twice the largest non-embedding parameter.
  - **Mode.** The session ran a direct reload.
  - **Sleep.** One case (`gpt-oss-mxfp4-tp1-sleep`) runs each reload inside a level-2 sleep: `sleep(level=2)`, then `wake_up(["weights"])`, then the reload, then `wake_up(["kv_cache"])`. It runs the same checks and also asserts that the engine slept and is fully awake again. gpt-oss is used because post-load processing reruns from state that level 2 must keep: the TRT-LLM MXFP4 permute indices (#66010).
  - **Outputs.** Reloaded A decodes exactly as cold A did on the same engine (tokens and logprobs). Reloaded B is close to fresh B (`check_logprobs_close`, separate engines). This catches values frozen into captured graphs or held where the walk can't see.
- **"Every tensor and scalar"** covers the registered parameters and buffers (shared-weight partitions and wrapper subclasses expanded), plus everything reachable from module attributes, breadth first up to 8 hops. That includes quant methods, kernels, the `nn.Module`s they hold outside the module tree, and host floats on attention impls. Engine and model configs are not walked.
  - KV/Mamba caches and EPLB load statistics are compared by address only.
  - Excluded from the comparison: direct-mode bookkeeping (absent in the layerwise reference), compile-cache paths, and one config memo.
  - The walk must find a compared off-registry tensor on every rank.
- **B is derived from A** unless a case names it:
  - every tensor is rolled by one along dim 0;
  - BF16/FP16/FP32 tensors are also scaled by 3, which changes every maximum;
  - constant tensors get an offset that no other constant of their dtype has, so duplicates diverge.

  Checkpoint tensors equal in A and B fail the test, except integer metadata such as `weight_shape`.
- **It catches real regressions:**
  - With #64692's in-place refill reverted, the DeepSeek-V3 FP8 cases fail. The CUTLASS stride tensors move and new allocator blocks appear on every reload, while every checksum matches.
  - An FP8-KV case (Llama-3.2-1B FP8-KV) found a bug on main: FlashInfer keeps the `bmm1_scale`/`bmm2_scale` of the first forward after a reload changes `k_scale`/`v_scale`. #65353 fixes it, so the case is left out here and lands with #65353 (see Validation).
  - The gpt-oss sleep case fails on main before #66010: level 2 drops the TRT-LLM permute-index cache, and the rerun rebuilds it differently (job 46799).
- **Cases** are data: `RefitCase(family, quant, model, parallel=..., model_b=None, engine=..., marks=...)`, with test id `<family>-<quant>-<layout>`. Multi-GPU cases carry `pytest.mark.distributed(num_gpus=N)`. Under Buildkite, a case that finds too few GPUs fails rather than skips.

  | Family | Quant | Checkpoint A | Covers | Layouts |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | qwen3 | bf16 | `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` | dense, tied embeddings | tp1 |
  | qwen3 | fp8-block | `inference-optimization/Qwen3-0.6B-FP8_BLOCK` | FP8 block linear | tp1 |
  | qwen3 | w4a16 | `inference-optimization/Qwen3-0.6B-W4A16-G128` | Marlin repack | tp1 |
  | deepseek-v3 | bf16 | `inference-optimization/DeepSeek-V3-debug-empty` | MLA, BF16 MoE (TRT-LLM) | tp1 |
  | deepseek-v3 | fp8 | `…-debug-empty-FP8_DYNAMIC` | MLA, FP8 MoE (CUTLASS) | tp1, tp2, tp2-ep, tp2-ep-eplb, dp2-ep |
  | deepseek-v3 | nvfp4a16 | `…-debug-empty-NVFP4A16` | NVFP4 weight-only MoE | tp1 |
  | gpt-oss | mxfp4 | `openai/gpt-oss-20b` | padded MoE (#64352), TRT-LLM MXFP4 (pinned with `moe_backend`) | tp1, tp1 sleep |
  | nemotron-h | bf16 | `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-4B-BF16` | Mamba2 + attention hybrid | tp1 |

  The EPLB layouts run with 2 redundant experts and no rebalance.
- **CI, and when each step runs:**
  - `:nvidia: (B200) Weight Reload Refit` (1 GPU, 45 min) runs automatically on PRs that touch the reload code the test drives: `model_loader/reload/`, `weight_utils.py`, `weight_checksum.py`, `distributed/weight_transfer/`, `model_executor/utils.py`, `parameter.py`, the worker's update session (`gpu_worker.py`, `extensible_kv_cache.py`), `device_allocator/` (sleep mode), `model_loader/utils.py` (record and rerun), the gpt-oss path (`fused_moe/`, `quantization/mxfp4.py`, `quantization/utils/mxfp4_utils.py`, `models/gpt_oss.py`; the per-PR gpt-oss case is the only gpt-oss reload check), and the test files. It runs:
    - `test_direct_reload.py` and `test_load_plan.py`, which no NVIDIA step runs while Model Executor is commented out;
    - the core cases (`-m "not distributed and not slow_test"`): qwen3 fp8-block, deepseek-v3 fp8, gpt-oss mxfp4 (plus its sleep variant), and nemotron-h bf16.
  - `:nvidia: (B200) [Nightly] Weight Reload Refit Extra Cases` (1 GPU) runs the `slow_test` cases: qwen3 bf16 and w4a16, deepseek-v3 bf16 and nvfp4a16.
  - `:nvidia: (2xB200) [Nightly] Weight Reload Refit` (2 GPUs) runs the `distributed` cases.
  - Both nightly steps are `optional: true`, following the repo's `[Nightly]` steps: they don't start on PRs, so start them by hand, or they run in nightly/full builds. They share a broad dependency list through a YAML anchor (quantization, MoE, attention, linear kernels, EPLB, the model files).
  - All steps export `VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn` and `PYTHONFAULTHANDLER=1` and use a per-test `--timeout`. Every utility RPC has a timeout.
- **`test_reload_moe_kernels.py`** loses its gpt-oss case, which the per-PR gpt-oss refit case covers with stricter checks. It also loses the output comparison only that case used. The Qwen3-NVFP4 CuteDSL case still checks addresses.
- **Determinism.** The fresh and refit engines compile separately, because their model paths differ, and Inductor's reduction autotuning can pick different configs for them. A strong perturbation like ×3 turns that last-bit difference into different greedy tokens.
  - The engines therefore set `compilation_config.inductor_compile_config={"deterministic": True}`, which is vLLM's documented way.
  - `TORCHINDUCTOR_DETERMINISTIC` set from the test is read at import and reset by the first compiled frame, so it doesn't work.
  - Compile state that differs between a cached and a fresh compile is excluded from the comparison.

## Validation

**Latest, at df14510110 (job 48048).** Same setup as below; the whole refit file in parallel arms on one node. Later commits rewrite `_last` for ruff, merge main (dropping the removed MTP completeness-check helper), and remove the llama-fp8-kv case; they were not rerun on GPU.

title: [Bugfix][Distributed] Order packed NCCL loads after the caller stream
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

`packed_nccl_broadcast_consumer` receives and loads on its own slot streams, which never wait on the caller's stream. Work the caller queued just before the receive can therefore run after the loads and overwrite them. In direct reload, that work is the zero-fill of padded MoE params that `begin_direct_reload` queues at `start_weight_update` (#64352): if it lands late, the loaded weights end up zero.

The fix makes each slot stream `wait_stream(caller_stream)` once, before the first receive. This adds no host sync and covers anything queued before the call. The unpacked NCCL path and IPC already load on the caller's stream.

This PR used to also copy misaligned packed entries on unpack (#64936). That fix is the same `unpack_tensor` change as #65009 and #57665, so it was dropped here to keep one fix per PR.

## Timeline (main)

```
caller stream:  --[ zero-fill W ]------------------------->   (queued first, runs late)
slot stream:    ----------[ broadcast ]--[ load W ]-------->   (no wait on caller)
GPU order:      load W -> zero-fill W -> W == 0
```

With the fix the slot stream waits on the caller's stream first, so the order is always zero-fill, then load.

## Validation

- `TestPackedBroadcastRoundtrip` now loads like a direct reload: every roundtrip copies the received tensors into destinations that the caller zero-fills on its own stream behind a GPU sleep right before the receive, and checks them byte for byte (shape and dtype are asserted before each `copy_`, which would otherwise convert silently). Each case runs once to warm up, then once with the sleep, and asserts the fill was still pending at the first load, so the race window was really open. This replaces four copies of the produce/consume/verify code with one helper. GB200 job 50811: without the fix all 7 roundtrip cases fail in 3/3 runs; with the fix 7/7 pass in 3/3 runs. Whole `tests/distributed/test_packed_tensor.py` with the fix: 33 passed. Ruff 0.17.2 check and format pass.
- End to end (earlier revision with the same stream change, job 46524): gpt-oss-20b, MXFP4, TP1, direct reload over packed NCCL, with a ~10 s GPU delay injected before begin's padding fill.
