title: [Model Loader] Direct reload of online-quantized modules
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

Direct weight reload (`VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, #64336) now supports online quantization on a BF16 checkpoint. Part of #54477 (F4).

This revision replaces the earlier layerwise-staging approach: no module is staged on meta, buffered, or re-quantized at `finish`. Online quantization in direct mode is a pre-quantized checkpoint method whose loaders quantize on arrival. The diff against main is 10 files: about +200/-10 of source, plus tests and docs.

## Problem

`VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct` refuses online quantization. Online methods create BF16 parameters on the meta device and quantize them in post-load processing. A direct reload writes in place into the kernel tensors, and those cannot hold BF16, so there is nothing to load the update into.

## Design

The only place a high-precision tensor can become a quantized one is the place it arrives: the weight loader.

- **Only in direct mode.** With `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct` (and not for requantization), `OnlineQuantizationConfig.get_quant_method` returns the method of the matching pre-quantized checkpoint for a convertible scheme. Every other mode keeps the online classes, so behavior there is unchanged from main.
- **Online scheme = checkpoint method + quantize-on-load.**
  - `quantize_on_load` wraps the weight loaders once and permanently. Each arriving tensor is quantized, then its values and scales are written through the original loaders.
  - Cold start and direct reload therefore load and post-process exactly like that checkpoint. There is no layerwise staging.
  - The full unsharded tensor is quantized before the original loader TP-splits it, as a checkpoint would be.
- **Scheme mapping** (linear / MoE):
  - `fp8_per_tensor` → `Fp8LinearMethod` / `Fp8MoEMethod`
  - `fp8_per_block` → the same, with 128×128 blocks
  - `fp8_per_channel` → `ModelOptLinearMethod` (PcPt) / `CompressedTensorsW8A8Fp8MoEMethod`
  - `mxfp8` → `ModelOptLinearMethod` / `CompressedTensorsW8A8Mxfp8MoEMethod`
  - `mxfp4` MoE → `Mxfp4MoEMethod`
  - `nvfp4_per_token` MoE → `ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoE` with the per-token override
- **NVFP4 pairing (the only special case).** w1 and w3 of an expert share one global scale. One w13 loader holds the first of the pair until the other comes, then quantizes both with the shared amax.

## Files

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `online/loading.py` (new) | `quantize_on_load`, the scheme → checkpoint-method mapping, NVFP4 w1/w3 pairing |
| `online/base.py` | In direct mode, return the checkpoint method, or raise for a scheme that has none |
| `base_config.py` | In direct mode, raise for requantization |
| `config/vllm.py` | Drop the blanket online-quantization refusal |
| `gpt_oss.py` | Refuse quantize-on-load layers: gpt-oss writes BF16 experts outside their loaders |
| `tests/quantization/test_online_loading.py` (new) | NVFP4 pairing (either order, a repeated half, other ranks' experts, a lone half), contiguous quantizer input |
| `test_direct_reload.py` | A quantize-on-load case in the reload-equals-cold-start suite |
| `docs/training/layerwise.md`, `docs/features/quantization/online.md` | Usage, supported schemes, refusals, NVFP4 delivery rule |

**NVFP4 pairing details.** The held half is a copy, because a weight-transfer receive buffer is reused. A packed NCCL transfer runs loads on alternating streams, so the pairing load waits on an event recorded after the copy and records its stream on the held tensor. A repeated half replaces the held one. Another rank's expert returns `False` before anything is held. If a half is still held at post-load processing, the update fails.

## Refused in direct mode

These raise at model construction, when the quant method is chosen:

- Online schemes without a quantize-on-load checkpoint method:
  - `mxfp4` linear, including `mxfp4_hadamard32`
  - any `hadamard_size`
  - `int8` / experts_int8
  - `lut_b`
  - lm_head targets
- An activation override that differs from the scheme default.
- Requantization of a pre-quantized checkpoint.
- gpt-oss with online quantization.
- `fp8_per_block` linear layers whose TP shards are not multiples of 128. `Fp8LinearMethod` validates the block shape, whereas main's online method pads.
- The NCCL load plan (`check_plannable`): tracing would quantize the traced tensors.
- The existing refusals in direct reload (`_check_supported_modules`, `VllmConfig._verify_direct_reload_compat`) are unchanged and stay as the backstop: Muse Spark FP8 MoE, fused shared experts, torchao, LoRA, weight offloading, Humming.

## Known differences and risks (direct mode only)

- **fp8_per_tensor numerics.** Each shard of a merged layer (q/k/v, w1/w3) gets its own scale. Post-load processing then requantizes to the max scale, exactly as for an FP8 checkpoint. Main's online path quantizes the merged BF16 weight once. The final scales are equal; values may differ by one extra FP8 rounding.
- **fp8_per_channel and nvfp4_per_token** quantize with the online path's own functions, so their values and scales match main.
- **Kernel selection follows the checkpoint method:**
  - fp8 MoE: `Fp8MoEMethod` disallows vLLM CUTLASS.
  - mxfp4 MoE: `select_deepseek_v4_mxfp4_moe_backend` prefers MXFP8, then BF16, activations (W4A8 / W4A16). Main's online method runs `kMxfp4Dynamic` (W4A4).
  - per-channel linear: ModelOpt's `select_linear_kernel`, without the online PTPC refusal of weight-only Marlin/Humming kernels.
- Experts loaded as one 3-D tensor (Llama 4 fused BF16 checkpoints) fail loudly in the 2-D quantizers. mxfp8 is the exception and loads.
- To be measured: GSM8K and decode tok/s against main's online cold start on flagship MoE models.

## Tests

In progress: unit tests (`test_direct_reload.py`, `test_online.py`), plus end-to-end L2 sleep → weight update → wake runs for every converted scheme on Qwen3-30B-A3B and flagship BF16 MoE models. Each run compares GSM8K and tensor digests with a fresh start, and decode throughput with main's online cold start. Results will be posted here.

title: [RL][Model Loader] Load FP8 indexer wk and MLA projections independently, as FP8 or BF16, in any scale layout
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Load the FP8 weights of layers that vLLM runs in BF16 (the sparse-attention indexer's `wk`, GLM5-next's MLA projections) from their own checkpoint parameters, so a weight and its scale can arrive in different `load_weights` calls, and accept the weight whole in BF16 as most RL trainers send it. Part of the direct weight reload work (#54477). Supersedes #64717.

Builds on aoshen02's restructuring of every indexer (aoshen02/vllm#243): `wk` and `weights_proj` are ordinary layers loaded under their own names, and `wk_weights_proj` (the fused BF16 GEMM) is a derived weight refilled in place after each load. No pending dicts, no merged-name mappings. This PR adds the input formats real trainers and checkpoints use on top of that structure.

## Files

- `vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/dequant_linear.py` (new): `DequantLinearMethod`, a layer with an FP8 checkpoint weight that runs in BF16. `wrap(layer)` converts a layer built by any quant config whose weight is FP8 (not online-quantized); `bf16_linear(build, quant_config)` builds a layer that way or, for another quantized format, unquantized. Also the loader that keeps a weight in the dtype it is sent in (FP8 or BF16) and the post-load dequantization.
- `vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/quant_utils.py`: `get_and_maybe_dequant_weights` returns a `DequantLinearMethod` layer's weight as is (it is BF16 after loading).
- `vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py`: `init_indexer_wk_weights_proj` builds `wk` (with `bf16_linear`) and `weights_proj` as checkpoint layers whose weights are views of the fused BF16 `wk_weights_proj`; `fuse_indexer_wk_weights_proj` refills it in place after each load.
- `vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_v2.py`, `vllm/models/deepseek_v32/*`, `vllm/models/hy_v4/*`, `vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_mtp.py`: use those two functions; drop the FP8 `wk` pairing and dequantization in `load_weights`.
- `vllm/models/glm5next/common/attention.py`: the indexer as above; the MLA projections are built with the checkpoint's quant config through `bf16_linear`.
- `vllm/models/glm5next/common/model.py`, `mtp.py`: drop the pending-dict FP8 pairing; `_mla_proj_checkpoint_tensor` adapts each tensor on its own (Quark scale name, NoPE `kv_a` padding of weight and block scale); match `modules_to_not_convert` by suffix.
- `vllm/models/dots3_note/nvidia/model.py`: its FP8 indexer `weights_proj` is wrapped with `DequantLinearMethod.wrap` instead of being dequantized in `load_weights`.
- `tests/quantization/test_fp8_dequant.py` (new, replaces `test_deepseek_v32_weight_loading.py` and the GLM5-next part of `test_quark.py`); `.buildkite/test_areas/quantization.yaml` runs it.
- `vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/fp8.py` is unchanged.

## Claims

- **BF16 `wk` (and BF16 MLA projections) from a trainer load correctly.** On #243 a BF16 tensor is cast into the FP8 parameter and dequantized with the previous update's scale: wrong values, no error. Here the weight is kept in the dtype it is sent in, and the scale is not needed for that update. FP8 ↔ BF16 can alternate between updates, in cold start, direct reload and layerwise reload, at the cold-start addresses.
- **Every `wk` scale layout found in published checkpoints dequantizes exactly:** 128×128 blocks (official DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.x FP8), per-channel `[128]` (Quark, amd/GLM-5.2-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8), MX 1×32 E8M0 (ModelOpt MXFP8), and E8M0 block scales under `Fp8Config`. On #243 the Quark per-channel `wk` fails at cold start (`AssertionError` in `get_and_maybe_dequant_weights`' identity-GEMM fallback, `ReplicatedLinear` has no `input_size_per_partition`).
- Weight and scale load independently, in either order and in different calls.
- **The fused indexer weight is filled on every path:** under a KV-cache quant method on the MLA layer (ModelOpt, e.g. nvidia/GLM-5.3-NVFP4, where #243 leaves it uninitialized), and after an in-place reload of the runtime weights (`refresh_derived_weights`). `wk` stays exact BF16 under online quantization, as on main.
- MiMo-V2's split loading is out of scope (its fused qkv is a separate problem).

## Validation

All on GB200, nightly wheel e336407a3d (= this branch's merge-base) with each arm's Python files overlaid. "Main" = e336407a3d, "#243" = cc96c04bea (aoshen02's head), "this PR" = c7b8cd58ce for the GPU runs below; 5d69c2f057 (review fixes) and 1bbe0fd507 (no extra memory) were checked with the unit tests, the memory table, the GLM-5.3-Flash reload and the DeepSeek-V3.2-NVFP4 check below.

## Details

**What RL trainers send for `wk`** (from reading each repo's weight-sync code):

| Framework | `wk` sent as | `weights_proj` |
|---|---|---|
| SkyRL (GLM-5 spec, `weight_sync/fp8/models/glm5.py`) | BF16 | BF16 |
| NeMo-RL default (quantizes in the vLLM worker per what vLLM built) | BF16 | BF16 |
| ROLL (`roll/third_party/vllm/fp8.py`), prime-rl (online FP8), vLLM `examples/rl/rlhf_http_nccl.py` | BF16 | BF16 |
| slime (`quantizer_fp8.py`, SGLang rollout) | FP8 + block `weight_scale_inv` | BF16 |
| verl native FP8 | FP8 + scale | — |

No trainer mixes FP8 and BF16 rows inside one tensor, so a tensor is accepted whole in one format.

**How published checkpoints store `wk`** (safetensors headers of 465 repos):

| Layout | Examples |
|---|---|
| Block FP8 128×128, F32 `weight_scale_inv` | deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2 (+Exp, Speciale), zai-org/GLM-5.x-FP8, zai-org/GLM-5.3 |
| BF16 | zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash (even the FP8 repo), most NVFP4/MXFP4 quantizations |
| MXFP8 1×32, U8 E8M0 `weight_scale` | local-inference-lab/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4-*, nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-FP4-Local (MTP layer), zianglih/DeepSeek-V3.2-MXFP8 |
| Per-channel `weight_scale` `[128]` | amd/GLM-5.2-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8 (F32), amd/DeepSeek-V3.2-mtp-ptpc (BF16) |
| Per-tensor | none |

**Design.**
- `DequantLinearMethod` (`quantization/dequant_linear.py`, not tied to `Fp8Config`) wraps the checkpoint's own linear method instead of subclassing `Fp8LinearMethod`. That method's `create_weights` makes the checkpoint parameters (names, shapes, loaders), so each loads on its own. `wrap(layer)` is the only entry point: the indexer's `wk`, GLM5-next's MLA projections and dots3's `weights_proj` are built with the checkpoint's quant config (so its ignored layers apply as for any layer) and wrapped when their weight is FP8, whatever the config: `Fp8Config`, Quark, ModelOpt MXFP8. `bf16_linear` rebuilds a layer of another quantized format unquantized (e.g. online quantization), as these layers are BF16 on main.
- `wrap` skips a layer that quantizes the BF16 tensors it loads (`quantizes_on_load`, online quantization in direct reload, #65802): viewing its FP8 weight in the sent dtype would store unscaled values.
- The weight's loader views the parameter in the dtype the tensor is sent in (FP8, or the model dtype) before the normal loader runs. After a cold start the parameter's storage is BF16-sized, so the view fits and direct reload keeps the address; at a cold start from an FP8 checkpoint the first BF16 load allocates.
- No extra memory. `wk` and `weights_proj` have no storage of their own: `weights_proj.weight` is a view of the fused weight's rows after `wk`'s, and `wk.weight` is a view of the start of the fused storage in the dtype it loads (FP8 or BF16). An FP8 weight (indexer `wk` or a GLM5-next MLA projection) is allocated BF16-sized and dequantized through a temporary back into that storage, so `wk` lands in its fused rows in every load mode; filling the fused weight then copies nothing. A part in its own storage (dots3's separately built `weights_proj`, or parameters handed over by the weight cache IPC loader, for which the fill also allocates the fused weight) is copied into the fused rows. Direct reload views `wk` back to FP8 on the same storage at begin.
- The BF16-accepting loader is a method bound to the layer, so layerwise reload's metadata (`sanitize_layer_refs`) does not keep layers alive. `wk` is built plain BF16 when the checkpoint does not store it in FP8.
- GLM5-next matches `Fp8Config`'s `modules_to_not_convert` by suffix (as `bailing_moe_v3`): GLM-5.3-Flash lists its BF16 modules under text-model names (`model.layers.N…`), which sit under `language_model.` in the multimodal model, so the exact match never applied and the BF16 indexer `wk` was built as an FP8 layer with a scale the checkpoint lacks. It is now built BF16: the probe counts 33 `Fp8DequantLinearMethod` (now `DequantLinearMethod`) per rank instead of 44 and 11 more `UnquantizedLinearMethod` (cold-start A/B against ebf9a34202, job 46735: GSM8K 0.9189 → 0.9196, KV cache 2.106M both).
- `DeepseekV32Attention` runs its indexer's post-load hook itself: `finalize_model_weights` does not descend into a layer that has a quant method, and ModelOpt gives every MLA layer a KV-cache method. Indexers also expose that hook as `refresh_derived_weights`.
- Post-load processing dequantizes an FP8 weight with whatever scale was loaded (`weight_scale_inv` or `weight_scale`; U8 read as E8M0; 1-D per channel, or per tensor with one scale per merged shard (`logical_widths`); group shape from `weight_block_size` or from the scale's shape) in one fp32 pass, and retires every scale. A BF16 weight is left as is. This replaces the block-only loop of #243 and the generic identity-GEMM fallback for these layers. `scaled_dequantize` is not used: GLM5-next's `fused_qkv_a_proj` ends in a partial block (e.g. 2048 + 576 rows), which its divisibility asserts reject. The temporaries (an fp32 copy and the expanded scale, about 8 bytes per weight element) live only while one layer is processed.

**Trade-offs and limits.**
- **Deferred to a follow-up (AMD Quark):** `amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4` stores the GLM5-next MLA projections as block FP8 with Quark's `weight_scale`. Main dequantized them in `load_weights` (#56176). Here they are now built with the checkpoint's config (Quark per-block FP8) and wrapped, as `wk` is, but `_mla_proj_checkpoint_tensor` pads the NoPE `kv_a` block scale only under the `weight_scale_inv` name, so the `kv_a` scale shard still fails its shape check at load. Not run end to end; the follow-up pads `weight_scale` too and validates that checkpoint.
- A fused parameter (GLM5-next `fused_qkv_a_proj`) must receive all its shards in one format within an update.
- When `wk` or an MLA projection arrives in BF16 its scale keeps the previous value; it is retired and unused, but still counts toward the layer's size. Layerwise reload therefore buffers that layer until finish, and the sharded RDT engine refuses it. Direct reload over NCCL/IPC is unaffected. This only concerns a trainer sending BF16 for a layer the checkpoint stores in FP8 (no longer GLM-5.3-Flash's `wk`, which is BF16 in the checkpoint and now built BF16). Deferred with the item above.
- No in-scope checkpoint with an MXFP8 `wk` runs end to end: the ModelOpt `MIXED_PRECISION` GLM-5.3-Flash checkpoints (local-inference-lab/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4-Spark, nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-FP4-Local MTP layer) also store `weights_proj`, `wq_b` and the MLA projections in MXFP8 / FP8 blocks, while GLM5-next builds those layers unquantized (main and #243 alike) and keeps building `wk` from `Fp8Config` only. Supporting them is a separate change; the MXFP8 dequantization itself is unit-tested here.
- `zianglih/DeepSeek-V3.2-MXFP8` names its MX scale `weight_scale_inv`, which ModelOpt MXFP8's parameter (`weight_scale`) does not match; untested, 23 downloads.
- MiMo-V2: out of scope.

## Overview

gpt-oss reload fixes for direct weight reload (`VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, #64336) and weight transfer. PR 10 of the direct weight reload stack (#54477).

1. gpt-oss experts streamed one at a time (#52209) are split across TP the way the full-checkpoint loader splits them.
2. gpt-oss stops zeroing the caller's `w2_bias` tensor.

The FlashInfer bmm-scale and TRTLLM prefill k/v-scale fixes that were in this PR moved to their own PR (#68032).

## Claims

- **Streamed gpt-oss MXFP4 experts at TP > 1 now match a fresh start.** The per-expert loader narrowed each rank's slice by the parameter's padded size. The MXFP4 backends pad each rank's intermediate size, so every rank but rank 0 took the wrong checkpoint rows. It now splits in whole MXFP4 blocks, as `_load_weights_mxfp4` does. Unquantized and NVFP4 experts use the same split with a block size of 1.

title: [RL][Model Loader] Direct reload: check that an update loaded every parameter
body:
## Overview

A direct weight reload (`VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, #64336) now checks at `finish_weight_update` that the update loaded every parameter cold start loaded. If any is missing, `finish` raises and names it, before post-load processing runs. Part of the direct weight reload work (#54477, F2).

On main, a parameter the update leaves out keeps its runtime bytes. `begin` views them as checkpoint bytes, and `finish` reruns post-load processing over them. That is silent corruption whenever the processing changes the layout or isn't idempotent (transposes, requantization, packing). Padded MoE parameters are worse: `begin` zero-fills them (`padding_fill_params`), so leaving one out serves zeros.

## Design

- **Required:** the parameter names cold start's `model.load_weights` returned (`track_loaded_params`, recorded by `record_checkpoint_layout`).
- **Delivered:** the names this update's `load_weights` calls returned between `begin` and `finish`, plus the tensors written without `load_weights`:
  - M2N's in-place writes;
  - the load plan's direct copies (`load_planned`, #65235).
  
  Both report through `mark_loaded`. The load plan's trace of `load_weights` loads nothing, so it is kept out of the record.
- Names are resolved to parameter objects before comparing, so a tied parameter counts under either name. Fused and per-expert checkpoint names both count, because `load_weights` reports parameter names.
- **Exempt:** parameters matching `--sleep-preserve-parameter-names`. Level 2 sleep keeps exactly the tensors an update doesn't rewrite, so they are the ones an update may leave out (e.g. the DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram tables). There is no new knob.
- **Dummy start:** cold start loaded nothing, so the first update sets the record and isn't checked itself. Requiring every parameter would reject correct updates, because some parameters are never sent: online-quantization scales are filled as a side effect of loading the weight, and fp8 KV-cache scales may be absent from the checkpoint.
- A `load_weights` that returns `None` turns the check off for that model.

**Not caught:** a partial shard or expert inside a parameter that the update did write, and wrong values. Checksums (#59371) cover values.

**Behaviour change.** Partial direct updates that ran on main now raise. For example, a trainer that keeps the vision tower frozen and doesn't send it must either send it or list it in `--sleep-preserve-parameter-names`. After a refused finish the model needs a new full update, as after any failed finish.

Cold start, layerwise reload and non-direct mode are unaffected.

## Validation

**Unit tests** (GB200, nightly 60bd6dd2 with each arm's Python files overlaid; PR vs main on the same node):

`test_direct_reload.py`, `test_load_plan.py`, `test_reload_lifecycle.py` and `test_reload.py` (job 51474, head 099ed99c13):

| Arm | Passed | Failed |
|---|---|---|
| this PR | 173 | 1 |
| main ea8f3140ef | 170 | 1 |

The failure, `test_reload.py::test_kv_scale_reload`, is the same on both arms. The 3 extra passes are this PR's new tests.

- `test_direct_reload.py::TestUnsent`:
  - a parameter left out raises before post-load processing, and a following full update repairs the model;
  - after a dummy start the first update sets the record, and a later partial update raises;
  - a parameter matched by `--sleep-preserve-parameter-names` may be left out and keeps its bytes.
- `test_load_plan.py::test_planned_update_is_checked_for_completeness`: a full update through the load plan passes; one that leaves out a direct name raises.

title: [RL][Model Loader] Direct reload: models opt in; refuse known-silent paths
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Direct weight reload (`VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, #64336) is meant to become the default. Before that, a reload of a model or component that isn't known to work must be visible instead of silently serving wrong weights. This PR does four things:

- Models declare that they were validated. An update of an undeclared model logs a warning, so users can still try direct reload but are told its behavior isn't guaranteed.
- One shared check, `check_direct_reload_support`, runs when the weight-transfer engine is created and in `begin_direct_reload`, only in direct mode. It replaces the cold-start module check and the config-time refusals (except `sharded_rdt`), so a server that never updates starts with any configuration.
- Components and quant methods whose bugs the runtime checks can't see declare a refusal, which the check raises.
- `sparse_nccl`, which bypasses begin/finish, warns in direct mode instead of being checked. Part of the direct weight reload work (#54477).

## Claims

- **One protocol, three outcomes.** A new protocol `SupportsDirectReload` in `interfaces.py` has two fields, `supports_direct_reload: bool = True` and `direct_reload_unsupported_reason: str | None = None`. They are plain annotations rather than `ClassVar`, because refusals are also set on instances. A `supports_direct_reload(model_cls) -> bool` helper answers "validated?" only. `check_direct_reload_support` treats a model in one of three ways:
  - **Validated:** the model class lists `SupportsDirectReload` as a direct base. It reloads with no warning. The class the loader generates for expert substitution counts as the class it wraps.
  - **Refused:** any module, including the root model, or a module's `quant_method` sets `supports_direct_reload = False` with a `direct_reload_unsupported_reason`, on its class or on the instance. `False` is inherited. The check walks `named_modules()` and raises `RuntimeError: direct reload: <Module> is not supported (<name>): <reason>`. Without a reason the message says "no reason given".
  - **Neither:** it logs once per class and the reload proceeds: `direct reload: <Class> is not validated with direct reload (it does not declare SupportsDirectReload); correctness after a weight update is not guaranteed. Use VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=layerwise if outputs look wrong.`

  `QuantizeMethodBase` carries the same two fields as plain class attributes (not the protocol, which means "validated" for models; quantization doesn't import from models). The online linear/MoE bases and the humming linear/MoE methods set `False`, so the check has no type tests; the fused-shared-expert online loader check stays (its routed method is pre-quantized). The check runs on the object the update reloads: `get_model()` for in-place reload and the target-model engines, and the draft for draft updates, since `set_weight_update_target` makes the draft the engine's model.
- **`True` isn't inherited; `False` is.** A class is validated only if it lists the protocol among its own bases (`SupportsDirectReload in cls.__bases__`). Otherwise marking `Qwen3ForCausalLM` would also mark `DFlashQwen3ForCausalLM`'s subclasses, including LiLiCorr, which needs #65800. Pooling adapters and VL subclasses (e.g. `Qwen3MoeLLMForCausalLM`) are likewise not marked, so they warn until they are validated.
- **All refusals live in the shared check** (config, declared module and quant-method refusals, and begin's read-only checks: no recorded checkpoint layout, replaced parameters, storages too small), so each also fails at engine creation.
- **One check, two call sites, direct mode only.** `check_direct_reload_support(model, vllm_config=None)` (`reload/direct.py`) raises on the config refusals moved from `_verify_direct_reload_compat` (weight offload, torchao, online quantization config, LoRA, `draft_lm_head_quantization`; `vllm_config` defaults to the current config), then walks the modules once for declared refusals, and warns once per class for an unmarked model. It is called:
  1. when the worker creates the weight-transfer engine, uncached, on the target and the draft if there is one, so a refused model fails at startup before a trainer connects and waits in a collective (skipped for `sparse_nccl`);
  2. in `begin_direct_reload`, which caches only a pass that checked a config: later begins skip the walk, a refusal is raised again each time, so a refusal that clears at runtime (MiniMax mono decode turning off) passes at the next update.

  `reload_weights` now refuses a loader that cannot iterate weights by name and rewrites `model_config.model` / `model_weights` / `revision` only after `start_reload` succeeds, so a refusal leaves the model and config untouched. torchao records no checkpoint layout (its wrapper tensors have none), so its server starts and an update is refused. Kernel-format `reload_weights` (`is_checkpoint_format=False`) never calls `start_reload` and stays unchecked: it copies processed kernel tensors and doesn't rerun post-load processing, the same in every mode. The online-quantization check unwraps elastic EP's `FusedMoEModularMethod.old_quant_method`, so no cold-start record is needed. A server without `weight_transfer_config` that never calls `reload_weights` runs no check and logs no warning; LoRA or offload servers start in direct mode. `sharded_rdt` stays the one config-time refusal (its replay plan is baked by a layerwise dry run).
- **New component refusals (errors).** Each sets `supports_direct_reload = False` and a reason on the module, so the check needs no platform-specific imports.
  - Muse Spark MegaMoE experts (NVIDIA, also the hybrid subclass);
  - DeepSeek-V4 AITER MegaMoE experts (ROCm);
  - Step-5 MegaMoE experts (NVIDIA);
  - DeepSeek-V4 AMD `--monokernel` decode layers;
  - Muse Spark specialized decode and its DSpark draft. Their post-load hooks already raised at finish; now `begin` refuses before it changes the model;
  - MiniMax-M3 AMD mono decode and its DSpark mono drafter. Both are refused only while enabled: they set the fields on the model instance at runtime and clear them when the kernels turn off;
  - Qwen3.8 PLE disk offload (`Qwen4ExpPLEDiskOffloadEmbedding`): its rows are views of the cold-start checkpoint files, and its loader raises mid-load on a resent row.
- **`sparse_nccl` warns in direct mode.** Its patches skip `start/finish_weight_update`, so there is no model check and no post-load rerun. Its engine logs once that results may be wrong for models whose post-load processing re-lays out weights; it is not refused.
- **First marks:** `Qwen3ForCausalLM`, `Qwen3MoeForCausalLM`, `DeepseekV3ForCausalLM`, `FalconH1ForCausalLM`, `DFlashQwen3ForCausalLM` (draft), `NemotronHForCausalLM`, and `Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration` with its language model `Qwen4ExpForCausalLM` (NVIDIA). title: [Bugfix][RL] Don't re-tie word embeddings on direct reload
body:
## Overview

Don't re-tie word embeddings when a direct reload (`VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`) finishes. Part of the direct weight reload work (RFC #54477). This is item 4 of the [#64336 review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64336#discussion_r4429569227).

## Claims

- A direct reload no longer drops later `lm_head` updates after one update sends an `lm_head` equal to the input embeddings. This affects models whose config ties the embeddings while the checkpoint has its own `lm_head`.
- Direct finish no longer copies both vocab tables to the host on every update.
- Cold start, layerwise reload and the weight-cache loaders are unchanged.

## Validation

Qwen3-0.6B (its config ties the embeddings), 1x L4, nightly `cf5cea2`. Cold start on a checkpoint whose `lm_head` differs from the embeddings, then `reload_weights` with `lm_head == embed` (B), then with `lm_head == -embed` (C). Output of a worker-side check after each reload:

On main, direct mode. B re-ties, and C's `lm_head` is dropped (generation after C is identical to after B):

```
B: {"tied": true, "lm_head[0,:3]": [-0.00927734375, 0.03369140625, -0.07470703125], "embed[0,:3]": [-0.00927734375, 0.03369140625, -0.07470703125]}
C: {"tied": true, "lm_head[0,:3]": [-0.00927734375, 0.03369140625, -0.07470703125], "embed[0,:3]": [-0.00927734375, 0.03369140625, -0.07470703125]}
```

With this PR, direct mode. Greedy outputs after C are identical to layerwise mode on main:

```
B: {"tied": false, "lm_head[0,:3]": [-0.00927734375, 0.03369140625, -0.07470703125], "embed[0,:3]": [-0.00927734375, 0.03369140625, -0.07470703125]}
C: {"tied": false, "lm_head[0,:3]": [0.00927734375, -0.03369140625, 0.07470703125], "embed[0,:3]": [-0.00927734375, 0.03369140625, -0.07470703125]}
```

`collective_rpc("reload_weights")` wall time, one run each (main and this PR in separate jobs on the same L4 flavor):

| | Reload mode | B (s) | C (s) |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | direct | 0.823 | 0.736 |
| main | layerwise | 0.329 | 0.305 |
| this PR | direct | 0.309 | 0.212 |
| this PR | layerwise | 0.311 | 0.282 |

New tests on main:

```
FAILED tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py::test_direct_reload_keeps_lm_head_untied
FAILED tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_tying.py::test_direct_reload_keeps_cold_start_tying
======================== 2 failed, 1 warning in 46.25s =========================
```

With this PR:

```
tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py::test_direct_reload_keeps_lm_head_untied PASSED [ 50%]
tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_weight_tying.py::test_direct_reload_keeps_cold_start_tying PASSED [100%]
======================== 2 passed, 1 warning in 19.00s =========================
```

`test_weight_tying.py`, `test_direct_reload.py`, `test_reload_lifecycle.py` and `test_reload.py` with `-m '(not slow_test) and (not distributed)'`: 127 passed, 1 skipped, 1 failed. The failure is `test_reload_weights_with_lora_moe`, a CUDA OOM on the L4 that also fails on main. The NVIDIA Model Executor CI step is commented out, so these ran on the L4; the AMD MI300 Model Executor step selects them.

## Details

`finish_direct_reload` reruns `process_weights_after_loading`, which starts with `maybe_retie_word_embeddings`. If the new `lm_head` equals `embed_tokens`, the re-tie points `lm_head.weight` at the embedding parameter, and from then on `AutoWeightsLoader` skips `lm_head.weight` as an alias. Layerwise reload never calls this function.

The fix makes `maybe_retie_word_embeddings` run once per model, using a marker attribute on the model. Every other caller of `process_weights_after_loading` (`base_loader`, the weight-cache daemon, `ipc_loader`) gets a fresh model, so only direct finish's rerun is skipped, and the re-tie happens only at cold start. The weight-cache IPC loader copies only the EAGLE flags across processes, so the marker doesn't carry over and the IPC process still re-ties at load.

Not changed: a model tied at cold start (checkpoint `lm_head` equals the embeddings) still can't take a different `lm_head` from an update.

title: [Bugfix][Attention] FP8 KV cache on MLA loads checkpoint scales and follows reloads
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

An FP8 KV cache on MLA models (DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM) now uses the checkpoint's KV-cache scales, and keeps following them when a weight update changes them. Part of the direct weight reload RFC #54477 (tracker row 29). Fixes hao-aaron/vllm#8 and the MLA part of hao-aaron/vllm#14.

1. **Cold start (bug on main):** no checkpoint `k_scale` / `v_scale` reached an `MLAAttention` layer. Every MLA model ran its FP8 KV cache at scale 1.0, with only a warning.
2. **Update, eager / piecewise decode:** FlashInfer MLA, FlashInfer MLA sparse and Tokenspeed MLA cached their bmm (softmax / output) scales at the first forward.
3. **Update, FULL CUDA-graph decode** (the default under `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`):
   - FlashInfer MLA decode on trtllm-gen now reads its bmm scales from fp32 device tensors that are refilled in place after every load.
   - The MLA cache write no longer bakes a "scale is 1.0" shortcut into the captured graph.

The same FULL-graph fix for standard (non-MLA) FlashInfer trtllm-gen / XQA decode is left to a follow-up (see Follow-ups).

## Claims

- **Checkpoint KV scales load into MLA layers** (compressed-tensors, fp8 and ModelOpt). There were two causes.
  - compressed-tensors, fp8 and ModelOpt mixed-precision gave a KV-cache quant method only to `Attention`, so `MLAAttention` had no `q/k/v_scale` parameters. (ModelOpt FP8/NVFP4 already covered MLA.)
  - `AutoWeightsLoader` applies the quant config's cache-scale mapper first. The mapper rewrites every format (`self_attn.k_scale`, `self_attn.k_proj.k_scale`, `kv_scale`, ...) to `self_attn.attn.k_scale`. `maybe_remap_kv_scale_name` then sent that to `self_attn.attn.attn.k_scale` and dropped it. In MLA models it now moves `.attn.{q,k,v}_scale` to `mla_attn.mla_attn`. Standard-attention models are unchanged (the GPT-J `attn.k_scale` case keeps its mapping).
  - Evidence: on DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite-Instruct-FP8 with calibrated per-layer scales (0.036–0.118), main loads 1.0 in all 27 layers, and this PR loads the checkpoint values (22 distinct). `test_mla_loads_checkpoint_kv_scales` and `test_mla_after_cache_scale_mapper` fail on main and pass here.
- **bmm scales follow reloaded KV scales.** They are now derived at every forward from the layer's host floats, as `FlashInferImpl` does. The sparse impl keeps the `bmm1_scale` / `bmm2_scale` attributes that Kimi K3's specialized decode reads. Kimi K3's DSpark drafter, which read the dense impl's cached attributes, now calls `FlashInferMLAImpl.host_bmm_scales(layer)`.
- **FULL-graph decode follows reloads on FlashInfer MLA (trtllm-gen).**
  - With a quantized KV cache and the auto decode backend (trtllm-gen on SM100), the bmm1/bmm2 scales are passed as fp32 device tensors.
  - They are derived by a new hook, `MLAAttentionImpl.process_kv_scales_after_loading(layer)` (a no-op by default). `MLAAttention.process_weights_after_loading` calls it once the KV-cache quant method has set the scales.
  - The hook refills the tensors in place with `refill_derived` (RFC rule 3: derived state stays at its address).
  - The cute-dsl backend (DCP, head counts trtllm-gen can't tile) rejects tensor scales, so it keeps host floats.
  - GPU smoke test on FlashInfer 0.7.3 (the pinned version): each kernel was captured with fp32 tensor scales, the tensors were changed in place, and the graph was replayed against eager host-float calls. The MLA trtllm-gen kernel matches exactly (max diff 0) at both scale settings, for backend `trtllm-gen` and `auto`, with and without the multi-CTA counter, at H=128/P=64 and H=16/P=32. Standard trtllm-gen (FP8 and BF16 query) and XQA match too. Jobs 47636 and 47637.
- **The MLA cache write always applies `k_scale`.**
  - `update_kv_cache` passed `skip_scale=(_k_scale_float == 1.0)`, a host bool that CUDA graphs capture. After a dummy start (scale 1.0) and a reload, captured decode steps wrote the cache unscaled while attention dequantized with the new scale (GSM8K 0.01).
  - Main never hit this, because MLA scales were always 1.0.
  - The same flag is dropped in DeepSeek V3.2's fused cache write (NVIDIA and ROCm). Dividing by 1.0 is exact, so a scale of 1.0 writes the same bytes.

## Validation

GB200, nightly wheel 827f2ccfaf (one commit below the base) with each arm's Python files overlaid, FlashInfer 0.7.3, `FLASHINFER_MLA`, FP8 KV cache, default `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`.

Model: `RedHatAI/DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite-Instruct-FP8` (27 MLA layers, Fp8Config). No small MLA checkpoint ships KV scales, so the harness adds them:
- calibrate per-layer amax of the MLA cache inputs with a BF16 KV cache on 70 prompts;
- add `model.layers.N.self_attn.{k,v}_scale = amax / 448` and `q_scale = 1.0` in a separate safetensors file.

GSM8K is 5-shot, 1319 questions, greedy.

Job 47676 (main = dce91fea6b, PR = b7cf875ff5). "PR − item 3" is the PR with the device-tensor path switched off in the harness overlay. "PR − cache-write fix" is the PR at c92c7b0640.

| Run | MLA `k_scale` in the layers | GSM8K |
|---|---|---|
| main, cold start, FP8 KV | 1.0 in all 27 layers | 0.768 |
| PR, cold start, FP8 KV | checkpoint values (0.036–0.114, 25 distinct) | 0.783 |
| PR, cold start, BF16 KV (reference) | n/a | 0.782 |
| main, dummy start → `reload_weights`, direct | 1.0 | 0.783 |
| **PR, dummy start → `reload_weights`, direct** | checkpoint values | **0.781** |
| **PR, dummy start → `reload_weights`, layerwise** | checkpoint values (BF16-rounded, see Limitations) | **0.782** |
| PR − item 3, dummy start → reload, direct | checkpoint values | 0.014 |
| PR − cache-write fix, dummy start → reload, direct | checkpoint values | 0.013 |

- With the PR, a reload under FULL CUDA graphs matches a cold start, and both are within noise of the BF16-KV reference.
- Without the device-tensor bmm scales, or without the cache-write fix, the reloaded engine decodes garbage. The dummy start captured scale 1.0 into the graphs.
- On main the reload "works" only because MLA never uses checkpoint scales at all.
- Greedy text isn't bit-identical between separate engines here, even main cold vs main reload, so the GSM8K score is the comparison. The CI test compares logprobs with `check_logprobs_close`.
- Earlier run 47662, before the cache-write fix: cold start main 0.776, PR 0.776–0.789, BF16 KV 0.786; every PR reload arm was 0.01. That run is how the cache-write bug was found.

**Tests** (same job; "main" = main plus this PR's tests):

| Test | main | PR − item 3 | PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_weight_utils.py::test_mla_after_cache_scale_mapper` (6 formats, new, CPU) | 6 failed | 6 passed | 6 passed |
| `test_mla_kv_scales.py::test_mla_loads_checkpoint_kv_scales` (new, compressed-tensors DeepSeek-V3 debug model) | failed: scales 1.0 | passed | passed |
| `test_mla_kv_scales.py::test_flashinfer_mla_decode_follows_kv_scale_reload[layerwise,direct]` (new, SM100) | 2 failed | 2 failed | 2 passed |

- The new tests run in a new `:nvidia: (B200) MLA KV-cache scales` step (`model_executor.yaml`). The NVIDIA Model Executor step is commented out on main.
- The cache-write fix has no CI test of its own. It only shows when the dummy start leaves the scale at exactly 1.0, as #65562 makes it; today the compressed-tensors dummy scales are random. The harness rows above cover it.

**Perf** (job 47663): `vllm bench throughput`, 256 prompts, 128 in / 1024 out, 64 concurrent seqs, FP8 KV, no checkpoint scales, 3 runs per arm with GPUs alternated.
- Output tok/s: main 12573 / 12608 / 12569, PR 12457 / 12395 / 12446. The PR is −1.2% (mean 12583 → 12433), consistent across runs and GPUs. The PR arm here is c92c7b0640; the later commits don't touch this path except dropping `skip_scale`.
- Cause: the tensor path adds one `bmm1 * log2e` op per layer per decode step inside FlashInfer, because the MLA API has no `bmm1_scale_log2` input. See Limitations.

## Limitations

- Standard (non-MLA) FlashInfer FULL-graph decode still bakes the startup bmm scales (hao-aaron/vllm#14). It is split into a follow-up because it rewrites the same `FlashInferImpl.forward` block as #65353 and #64329.
- FULL-graph decode still bakes host-float scales in these paths:
  - FlashInfer MLA's cute-dsl fallback (DCP, head counts trtllm-gen can't tile);
  - FlashInfer MLA sparse;
  - Tokenspeed MLA;
  - the Kimi K3 drafter / specialized decode.
  These paths now follow reloads in eager and piecewise decode only. FA2 decode and ROCm AITER asm decode can't take tensor scales; direct reload will refuse them (#66002).
- XQA MLA (`xqa_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla`) is SM120-only and isn't reached by `FLASHINFER_MLA` (SM100-only), so it wasn't run.
- About 1.2% decode throughput cost from the device-tensor scales (above).
- Giving `MLAAttention` a KV-cache quant method under fp8 / compressed-tensors also brings two side effects that `Attention` already has:
  - `finalize_model_weights` skips its children (as it already did under ModelOpt);
  - `fp8_e5m2` with an FP8 checkpoint is refused.
- Layerwise reload recreates KV scales in the model dtype, so reloaded scales are BF16-rounded (0.05329 vs 0.05322). This is on main for every attention type and is out of scope here; direct reload keeps them exact.
- `CUTLASS_MLA` refuses q/k scales other than 1.0 (`NotImplementedError`). With checkpoint scales now loaded, `--attention-backend CUTLASS_MLA` won't start on such checkpoints; `FLASHINFER_MLA` is the SM100 default.
- The opt-in FP8 prefill query quantization gathers context chunks from the FP8 cache without applying `k_scale`. This was correct only while MLA scales were 1.0.
- compressed-tensors gives MLA a KV-cache method only for a per-tensor `kv_cache_scheme`, because MLA has one latent head. Checkpoints without a scheme stay at 1.0, as on main.
- DeepSeek V3.2 / GLM-5 (DSA, where the MLA layer is `self_attn`) now load scales too. This wasn't GPU-validated.
- Only the DeepSeek-V2 model family was run. Other MLA models that call `maybe_remap_kv_scale_name` (bailing, glm4_moe_lite, AXK1, glm5next, kimi_k3 AMD) get the remap but weren't validated.

## Follow-ups

- Standard FlashInfer trtllm-gen / XQA FULL-graph decode scales as device tensors, stacked on #65353 (hao-aaron/vllm#14).
- FULL-graph device scales for FlashInfer MLA sparse (DeepSeek V3.2 / GLM-5) after a sparse-MLA smoke test.
- Pass a precomputed log2 bmm1 scale to the MLA kernel once FlashInfer exposes it, to remove the extra op.

title: [RL][Weight Transfer] Packed NCCL: one chunk layout for every side, opt-in wire segments for large tensors
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Packed NCCL weight transfer for RL (#54477): one chunk layout shared by every side, and opt-in wire segments so tensors bigger than the packed buffer no longer need a buffer of their size (fixes an OOM on 16 GiB expert stacks). This is aoshen02's #67838 (their commit, authorship kept) with review fixes on top.

The planned producer and planned receive that were also in this PR moved to their own draft, #68065, stacked on this one: their copy planning is expected to move into the load plan, which is still under discussion.

- **One chunk layout for every side.** `chunk_layout` derives the packed chunks from the metadata alone, with the `pack_tensors` rule, so the producer, the consumers and the trainer ranks that only relay always cut the stream the same way.
  - The producer fills each chunk with one `_foreach_copy_` into a buffer, then one broadcast.
  - Relaying trainer ranks receive each chunk into one buffer and drop it, without unpacking.
- **Wire segments, opt-in.** With segments on, a tensor over twice the buffer (one layer's expert stack, say) travels as dim-0 row ranges, so neither side needs a buffer of its size. Before, a 16 GiB expert stack needed 16 GiB buffers on the receiver and ran out of memory.

## Fixes on top of #67838

| Fix | Why |
|---|---|
| Wire segments are opt-in (`packed_wire_segments` in the NCCL init info), off by default | Segments change the wire layout. With them off, the layout is exactly `pack_tensors`'s (tested byte for byte), so a trainer or worker that predates segments, or a framework that reimplements the packing, keeps working. vLLM's trainer engine turns them on and tells the workers at init; the field is sent only when on. |
| The consumer's slot streams wait for the caller's stream before the first receive, and the producer's before each chunk; copies handed to `post_unpack_func` are `record_stream`ed like the packed buffer | #67838's rewritten consumer dropped the wait that main gained in #65487, so a load could run before work queued ahead of the receive (begin's padding fill) and be erased by it. |
| A split tensor is written segment by segment into one preallocated tensor of its full size | #67838 cloned every segment and concatenated them, about twice the tensor at peak. Now it's about one tensor plus the receive buffers (tested). |
| The trainer's layout cache is keyed on every name, shape and dtype | It was keyed on (length, first name, last name). |
| No hardcoded `"cuda"` device for packed buffers; a warning when one row is over the buffer (that tensor travels whole) | |

## Validation

Pending: job 51554 (GB200, nightly wheel b409a4f0d7 with this branch's Python files overlaid).

## Limitations

- Tensors between one and two buffers travel whole, so a chunk can reach about three buffers.
- A tensor whose single row is over the buffer travels whole (with a warning).
- No multi-node or TP>1 run here, so relaying trainer ranks are covered by unit tests and the earlier measurements in #67838.
- A worker that predates `packed_wire_segments` rejects the new field in vLLM's trainer init payload, unless the trainer turns segments off. That's a loud failure at init, not a hang.

title: [Bugfix][Attention] FlashInfer: bmm scales follow reloaded KV scales; TRTLLM prefill k/v scales applied once
body:
## Overview

Two FlashInfer fixes, split out of #65353 (the direct weight reload stack, #54477).

1. The FlashInfer bmm scales follow KV-cache scales that change on a reload, in prefill and in eager / piecewise-graph decode. FULL-graph decode still keeps the captured startup scales, as on main (see Limitations).
2. TRTLLM prefill with a BF16 query and an FP8 KV cache no longer applies the k/v scales twice (hao-aaron/vllm#9). This one is a cold-start bug.

## Claims

- **FlashInfer bmm1/bmm2 scales follow reloaded KV-cache scales in prefill and in eager / piecewise-graph decode.** They were computed once from the host-float q/k/v scales at the first forward and then never recomputed. A reload that changes `k_scale` / `v_scale`, such as the dummy start + real update RL flow with an FP8 KV cache, kept the warmup's values. They are now computed on every forward from the same host floats, as the other host-float scales in this backend already are. No host sync is added. `is_quantized_kv_cache` is evaluated once at init.
  - `test_reload.py::test_kv_scale_reload` fails on main on Blackwell, where FlashInfer is the default backend (prompt perplexity 6575, threshold 10). It passes with this PR.
  - In direct mode the same test (dummy start, then reload the FP8-KV checkpoint) fails on main and passes with this PR plus #65562 (the checkpoint has no `q_scale`, which otherwise keeps its random dummy value).
- **TRTLLM prefill with a BF16 query and an FP8 KV cache applies the k/v scales once.** This path first dequantizes the pages it reads with `trtllm_prefill_attn_kvfp8_dequant`, which already multiplies K by `k_scale` and V by `v_scale`. The kernel was then also given `bmm1_scale = scale · q_scale · k_scale` and `bmm2_scale = v_scale`, so k and v were scaled twice, and `q_scale` was applied to a query that was never quantized. Decode doesn't do this, so prefill and decode disagreed whenever the scales weren't 1.0. On this branch only, the kernel now gets `bmm1_scale = scale` and `bmm2_scale = 1.0`. The default FP8-query path is unchanged.
  - New test `test_flashinfer_trtllm_prefill_bf16_query_fp8_kv_scales` (`k_scale` 0.5, `v_scale` 2.0, `q_scale` 0.25) fails on main (67.5% of elements mismatched, max abs diff 0.88 against 0.06 allowed) and passes with the fix. The correctness helper now stores an FP8 cache's context with the layer's k/v scales and builds the reference the same way.
- **CI:** `test_reload.py::test_kv_scale_reload` now also runs in the existing `:nvidia: (B200) Quantized MoE` step, which gains dependencies on `quantization/kv_cache.py`, `attention/attention.py` and `test_reload.py`. CI doesn't run it on NVIDIA today: the NVIDIA Model Executor step is commented out.

## Validation

GB200, nightly wheels with each arm's Python files overlaid. The code is unchanged from #65353's last revision (416ea4ef34), re-applied on current main.

| Test | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `test_reload.py::test_kv_scale_reload` (existing) | fail: perplexity 6575 | pass |
| same test with `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, + #65562 on both arms | fail | pass |
| `test_attention_backends.py::test_flashinfer_trtllm_prefill_bf16_query_fp8_kv_scales` (new) | fail | pass |
| `test_attention_backends.py` (whole file) | 160 passed, 9 skipped, 18 failed | 161 passed, 9 skipped, 18 failed |

The 18 failures on both arms are the `microsoft/Phi-tiny-MoE-instruct` sliding-window cases, which can't load that model's config offline on this cluster. Jobs 49811 (after merging main into #65353), 47629 (the prefill fix: fails on main and without the fix, passes with it), 45214 / 45215 and 45235 / 45236 (`test_kv_scale_reload`, layerwise and direct).

**Cold start.** Qwen3-8B BF16, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention-backend FLASHINFER` (GB200, TP1): GSM8K 0.8704 → 0.8704, throughput 8262 → 8261 tok/s (FP8 query and KV cache with trtllm-gen decode, the path where the bmm scales are now computed every forward), KV cache unchanged (job 45300). gpt-oss-20b with `--attention-backend FLASHINFER` (TP2): 0.8832 → 0.8832, 14697 → 14778 tok/s (job 45299).

## Limitations (all on main too)

- FULL CUDA-graph decode (the default for trtllm-gen / XQA decode under `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`) bakes the host floats into the captured graph, so it keeps the startup scales after a reload. Fix: keep bmm1/bmm2 as device tensors refreshed on reload (hao-aaron/vllm#14); trtllm-gen accepts tensor scales.
- `_o_scale_float` (fused output quant) is computed once.

## Follow-ups

- FULL-graph decode bmm scales as device tensors (hao-aaron/vllm#14).
- MLA backends: same fix, validated on branch `mla-bmm-scales`; lands with MLA KV-scale loading (#66666).
- AITER asm decode builds its KV-scale tables once, so they go stale after a reload (hao-aaron/vllm#12).
- An FP8-KV case in the refit test (`test_reload_refit.py`), dropped from #65347 to land with this fix.

title: [Bugfix] Keep KV-cache scale defaults under dummy loading
body:
## Overview

With `load_format=dummy`, the dummy loader writes random values into the attention KV-cache scales. Checkpoints without KV-cache scales never overwrite them, so after a dummy start and a weight sync (the usual RL startup) they still differ from a real start. This PR makes dummy loading write the same values a real start has. Part of the direct weight reload work (#54477).

## Claims

- **Dummy start + sync now matches a real start for the attention scales.** The `KVCacheScaleParameter` scales (`q/k/v/prob_scale`) get the `-1.0` "not loaded" sentinel, the `_q/_k/_v/_prob_scale` buffers get `1.0`, and the compressed-tensors `q/k/v_scale` / zero points get `1.0` / `0.0`, all through the existing `dummy_weight_value` attribute. Post-load processing then takes the same "no checkpoint scales" path as on a real start.
- On Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 (TP4, `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`), the attention tensors that differ from a fresh real start after a dummy start + 1 sync drop from 1152 to 0 (auto KV cache) and from 768 to 0 (FP8 KV cache).
- Real (non-dummy) loading is unchanged: only the dummy loader reads `dummy_weight_value`.

## Validation

GB200, nightly wheel of d3a3230931 with this branch's Python files on top.

**Unit test**: `tests/quantization/test_fp8.py::test_dummy_load_keeps_kv_cache_scales_of_real_start[auto|fp8 × base|compressed_tensors]` (new, CPU-only). It builds a layer with real-start scales and one loaded by `DummyModelLoader`, runs post-load processing on both, and asserts exact equality of the state dict, the host float scales and the CPU scale copies.

| | main (job 44564) | this PR (job 44565) |
|---|---|---|
| new test, 4 cases | 4 failed: e.g. `_k_scale` expected 1.0, got -0.000942 (auto); `k_scale` expected -1.0, got -0.000942 (fp8) | 4 passed |
| `test_fp8.py -k "kv_cache or dummy or scale"` | | 25 passed |
| `test_compressed_tensors.py -k "kv_cache or attn_head"` | | 2 passed |
| `test_weight_utils.py` | | 57 passed |

```
pytest tests/quantization/test_fp8.py -k test_dummy_load_keeps_kv_cache_scales_of_real_start
```

**End to end**: Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8, TP4, `VLLM_RELOAD_MODE=direct`, `--max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.5`. A fresh real start is snapshotted, then a `--load-format dummy` start takes one full IPC weight sync from the same checkpoint. Every device tensor is compared with the fresh snapshot (runtime state excluded). GSM8K is 5-shot greedy over 1319 questions. A = main (d3a3230931), B = this PR, same node, back to back.

| KV cache | Arm | Tensors differing from fresh (dummy + 1 sync) | GSM8K real start | GSM8K dummy + 1 sync |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| auto | A (main) | **1152**: `{q,k,v,prob}_scale`, `_k_scale`, `_v_scale` × 48 layers × 4 ranks | 0.9030 | 0.8999 |
| auto | B (this PR) | **0** | 0.8984 | 0.8984 |
| fp8 | A (main) | **768**: `{q,k,v,prob}_scale` × 48 layers × 4 ranks | 0.8908 | 0.8863 |
| fp8 | B (this PR) | **0** | 0.8870 | 0.8870 |

A real start + 1 sync matches the fresh snapshot in both arms. GSM8K is within noise (main real starts range 0.899–0.908 across runs).

**CI**: the NVIDIA Quantization step in `.buildkite/test_areas/quantization.yaml` is commented out on main ("Disabled until torchao transitive dependencies are locked"), so CI will not run the new test on NVIDIA until it is re-enabled. The AMD mirror is commented out with it. The test needs no GPU.

## Details

**Root cause.** `DummyModelLoader` fills every parameter and persistent buffer through `initialize_single_dummy_weight`, which writes random values unless the tensor sets `dummy_weight_value`. The attention scales are never in a checkpoint without KV-cache scales:

- `q/k/v/prob_scale` (`KVCacheScaleParameter`) are created as `-1.0`, the sentinel post-load processing reads as "not loaded, use the default". After a dummy load they hold a random value. With one seed, that value is the same for all of them.
- `_q/_k/_v/_prob_scale` are persistent buffers registered at `1.0` by `set_default_quant_scales`. With an unquantized KV cache, post-load processing rewrites `_q_scale` and `_prob_scale` but not `_k_scale` / `_v_scale`, so those kept the dummy value.
- Compressed-tensors `q/k/v_scale` are created as `1.0` (zero points `0.0`) and used directly as the scales. A checkpoint without a `kv_cache_scheme` never writes them, so with an FP8 KV cache the random value became the scale.

A weight sync from such a checkpoint never writes these tensors, so the dummy values outlived it. Layerwise reload used to hide this by recreating the scales on every reload; direct reload writes in place and exposed it.

**Fix.** The fix sets `dummy_weight_value` to each tensor's creation value, the mechanism layernorm and ModelOpt already use:

- a class attribute on `KVCacheScaleParameter`, covering every method that uses `BaseKVCacheMethod.create_weights` (Fp8, ModelOpt, Quark, ...);
- the buffers in `set_default_quant_scales`, covering Attention, MLAAttention and the models that call it directly;
- `set_weight_attrs` in `CompressedTensorsKVCacheMethod.create_weights`.

On main, a dummy start with an FP8 KV cache kept GSM8K only because the shared random value happened to be negative and took the fallback to 1.0 (`_k_scale` / `_v_scale` match in the FP8 run above). A positive value would have become the KV-cache scale.

title: [Core] Tag multiproc executor RPCs with a sequence id to drop stale replies
body:
## Purpose

`MultiprocExecutor.collective_rpc` has no way to match a worker reply to the request it answers. Requests are `(method, args, kwargs, output_rank)` and replies are `(status, result)`, so each call assumes the next reply on each response queue is its own. That only holds if every call reads every reply it is owed. Two cases break it:

1. **A call times out.** The worker still posts its reply when it finishes. The next call reads that reply as its own. Under async scheduling, a probe-style RPC with a short timeout (e.g. a `check_health` broadcast with `timeout=10`) can time out during a transient worker stall such as runtime JIT/codegen. The next `sample_tokens` then reads the probe's `None` reply, and `step_with_batch_queue` raises `RuntimeError("unexpected error")`, which kills EngineCore. A stall of about 10s becomes a full engine restart. We hit this in production.
2. **A call fails partway.** `get_response` raises on the first `FAILURE` status, so the replies from the remaining ranks are never read. The next call on those ranks gets them instead. This is #49972; #49976 tried to fix it by draining the queues and was closed.

New callers keep hitting this. #59179 and #46811 add readiness probes that call `execute_dummy_batch` with a timeout and, on purpose, don't mark EngineCore dead when it fires. Without this fix, one such timeout corrupts the next model step.

## Changes

`vllm/v1/executor/multiproc_executor.py`:
- The executor tags each request with an id from a per-executor counter: `(seq, method, args, kwargs, output_rank)`.
- `WorkerProc` passes `seq` through `_execute_worker_rpc`, `handle_output`, the async-output thread's queue, and `enqueue_output`. Replies are now `(seq, status, result)`.
- `get_response` discards replies with an older `seq` and logs a warning for each. Replies are FIFO per worker, so a newer `seq` would be a protocol bug and is asserted against.
- Each discard re-checks the deadline, so skipping stale replies still counts against the caller's timeout.

`vllm/v1/executor/ray_executor_v2.py`: initializes the counter. `RayExecutorV2` inherits `collective_rpc` and the `WorkerProc` loops, so it gets the same fix.

Timeouts on model-path RPCs (`execute_model`, `sample_tokens`, ...) still propagate and stay fatal, as before. This PR only makes sure that a call that stops reading early can't corrupt the calls after it.

Overhead is one int per request and per reply.

## Duplicate check

Searched open and closed PRs for `stale response collective_rpc`, `MessageQueue response mismatch`, `rpc request id multiproc executor`, and `collective_rpc timeout desync`. Related work:
- #41357 (merged) clamps negative deadlines; it doesn't touch reply correlation.
- #49976 (closed) drained the queues on FT failure. This PR covers that case and timeouts with one mechanism.

No open PR adds request/reply correlation.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/executor/test_multiproc_executor.py tests/v1/executor/test_multiproc_executor_timeout.py -v
pre-commit run --from-ref upstream/main --to-ref HEAD
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files vllm/v1/executor/multiproc_executor.py vllm/v1/executor/ray_executor_v2.py
```

- New `test_collective_rpc_discards_stale_reply_after_timeout`: a call times out, the late reply arrives ahead of the next call's reply, and the next call must return its own result.
- Existing tests are updated for the new request/reply tuples. `test_execute_worker_rpc_returns_worker_exception` now also checks that `seq` is echoed back.

## Test Result

- 10 passed, and all pre-commit hooks and mypy pass.
- **Not yet run on GPU.** This changes the reply format on the hot path, so before marking it ready I'll run TP>1 serving with async scheduling, plus a run with a forced RPC timeout. Draft until then.
- This doesn't change model outputs, so no accuracy eval is needed.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to write this change. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.
